item.title: [field notes nyc] things to do in new york: nov 9 - 15
item.description: Open studios at ISCP, Sichuanese potluck and a very good week for talks (Triple Canopy symposium and more)
item.dc:creator: field notes nyc | Danielle
item.content:encoded:
Monday, November 9

🎞️ New York: A Documentary Film: Shadows of the Past Screening and Q&A
6—9pm | SVA Theatre: 333 W 23rd St, Manhattan | $11.49+

“Experience the newest installment of a sweeping narrative exploring the forces that shaped the city in the second half of the 20th century. The screening of Episode 9 will be followed by a talkback and Q&A with filmmakers Ric Burns and James Sanders, moderated by Cassim Shepard, Principal, SQ Projects and OHNY Board Member.”

💥 Civic Crash Course with Chloë Bass, Hal Foster & Jeremy Toussaint-Baptiste
7pm | Public Records: 233 Butler St, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“How do artists misunderstand the public, and vice versa? A conversation about destruction as criticism. The artists and Jeremy Toussaint-Baptiste often work in public: Bass has collaborated with civic agencies to create art for billboards and subway stations, while Toussaint-Baptiste has performed in parks and plazas with a cop car that he transformed into a sound system.”

Tuesday, November 10

🎧 Guest Speaker: Arthur Rieger of Hardwax at Head Hi
6—8pm | Head Hi: 146 Flushing Ave, Brooklyn | Donations $5+

“A new series of talks focusing on sound, design, music curation and critical aspects of the work done by experts dedicating their lives to the musical experience IRL.”

📻 A Benefit for La Voz Popular: Félix Zurita’s Caminos del silencio, introduced by Tobi Haslett
7pm | Light Industry: 361 Stagg St, Suite 407, Brooklyn | $10 donation

“Light Industry’s screening is a fundraiser for an effort to build a museum in the Guatemalan highlands dedicated to memorializing La Voz Popular.”

Wednesday, November 11

🎨 Art Week NYC (through Sat 11/14)
Times vary | Citywide: Midtown hub plus 80+ galleries and museums

“A four-day event inviting collectors, patrons, and art enthusiasts to experience the city’s vibrant art landscape.”

🏛️ Koichi Takada and Daniella Ohad: Design, Nature, and the Future
6—7:30pm | Museum of Arts and Design: 2 Columbus Circle, Manhattan | $25

“Join us for a thought-provoking conversation on the future of design, sustainability, and architectural culture with architect Koichi Takada and design historian ”

📷 Women as Witnesses: Photography and the Algerian Revolution
6:30—8pm | ICP Library: 84 Ludlow St, Manhattan | $5

“Women drove the Algerian Revolution (1954–62) as combatants, nurses, and photographers on the frontlines, yet their role remains largely overlooked.”

🏃 Reading 4 Sport: Good Sport NYC x READING 101
7pm | Night Club 101: 101 Avenue A, Manhattan | Free with RSVP | 21+

“Reading 4 Sport is a collaboration between and READING 101. It’ll be a night of athletics-related readings from five local writers.”

Subscribe now

Thursday, November 12

📚 An LGBTQ+ Author Panel with Antoni Porowski at Housing Works
5—7pm | Housing Works Bookstore: 126 Crosby St, Manhattan | price TBD

“Join Sad Dads Book Club and Surviving New York for a special evening celebrating LGBTQ+ writers, storytelling, and community, hosted by Emmy winner, NYT Bestselling cookbook author, and star of Queer Eye, Antoni Porowski. The evening will feature authors , , Temim Fruchter, and Mayukh Sen. Together, they’ll explore the stories we tell, the perspectives that shape contemporary literature, and the importance of creating space for LGBTQ+ voices.”

🤖 Sherry Turkle, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines, interviewed by Katie Hafner
6pm | Members’ Room, The New York Society Library: 53 E 79th St, Manhattan | $15

“From the author of prescient best seller and classic Reclaiming Conversation, Sherry Turkle, comes an urgent warning about how our ever-increasing reliance on human-like AI chatbots is eroding our capacity for empathy, caring, and the very qualities that make us human.”

🛜 Invisible Visible 未见之见 & Silenced Sunrise: Taiwan’s Music vs. the China Factor — Documentary Screening and Directors’ Q&A
6—8pm | Library for Arts & Culture: 10 Lafayette Ave, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“Join us for the screening of two documentaries, “Invisible Visible 未见之见” and “Silenced Sunrise: Taiwan’s Music vs. The China Factor”, for a look at how censorship shapes what people can see, hear, and say.”

🌿 Maya Lin on Art, Nature, and Memory
6:30—7:30pm | Asia Society: 725 Park Ave, Manhattan | $30

“Join us at Asia Society’s New York headquarters for a special evening featuring renowned artist and architectural designer Maya Lin.”

💸 Offsite: Mona Chalabi: Ten Lives w/ Jia Tolentino
7—8pm | First Unitarian Congregational Society in Brooklyn: 119 Pierrepont St, Brooklyn | $10.89+

“A visually striking exploration of money—and the lack of it—in America told through the lives of ten individuals, from a Pulitzer Prize–winning data journalist and artist.”

make plans w/ a friend!

Share

Friday, November 13

🖼️ First Fridays: Free Access to the “25th Anniversary Exhibition” at Neue Galerie
5—8pm | Neue Galerie: 1048 Fifth Ave, Manhattan | Free

🎞️ A Future Beyond Rikers: A Film Festival, Opening Night
5:30—9pm | Maysles Documentary Center: 343 Lenox Ave, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

A two-day gathering of film, storytelling, workshops, and community conversation.

🏙️ 2026 Fall Open Studios Opening Reception at ISCP
6—9pm | ISCP: 1040 Metropolitan Ave, Brooklyn | Free

“Fall Open Studios is a presentation of international contemporary art by the 33 artists and curators from 26 countries in residence.”

🎭 Every A-Side Has a B-Side with Ralph Lemon, Sol Cabrini, Taja Cheek, Jonathan González, Nile Harris, yuniya edi kwon & T. Lax
8pm | Roulette: 509 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“An evening of performances that consider the value of liveness and the spectre of commodification. On Value centers on the particular experience—as old as the commercialization and circulation of Black art in the United States—of being valued as a source of entertainment or art, transcendence or truth, while being discounted as a person. Reflecting on the efforts of institutions to collect, codify, and reproduce performance, the book considers the tensions between objects and bodies, presence and permanence.”

Saturday, November 14

🏙️ Site Conditions: Five Talks on Art and the City
11am—6pm | New Museum Theater: 235 Bowery, Manhattan | $15 per talk

For Art Week NYC, the New Museum and Artforum co-present a day of talks featuring artists, architects, filmmakers, critics, and writers. Working Conditions (12:30pm), with and Ajay Kurian, is the one I’m most curious about.

🚲 Brooklyn Cranksgiving 2026
12—4pm | Principles GI Coffee House: 139 9th St, Brooklyn | $50 donation

Brooklyn Cranksgiving is a scavenger-hunt-style bike ride that supports food access and equity in the community.

🌱 Garden the City: An Afternoon of Urban Ecology with LESCSS & LUPE
1—3pm | Private garden, then Brooklyn Bridge Park: address shared after RSVP| Free with RSVP

🎲 Bets in a Burning House with David Hill, Ayesha A. Siddiqi & Jacob Silverman
5pm | Roulette: 509 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“A conversation on the history and rise of prediction markets—and the costs of borrowing from the future.” Featuring , and .

Sunday, November 15

🗂️ Community Archiving Day at the Queens Museum
11am—4pm | Queens Museum: Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Queens | Free

"Everyone is welcome to this free event to learn about archival practice and preservation efforts taking place across NYC.”

🗽 Fighting for New York Author Event with Nicholas Freudenberg
3—5pm | Mil Mundos: 323 Linden St, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“Join Nicholas Freudenberg, Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Public Health at CUNY and author of Fighting for New York: Activism for Health and Social Justice Since the 1960s, for a conversation on the movements that have shaped New York City over the last six decades.”

🥢 Prospect Park Cookbook Club No. 4: The Food of Sichuan
3pm | 390 Social: 390 5th Ave, Brooklyn | $3

“Enjoy some warming spices for the chilly weather - we’ll be featuring Fuchsia Dunlop’s The Food of Sichuan!”

🎨 The Battleground of Art: Marco Baravalle and Gregory Sholette, moderated by Hallie Ayres
4pm | Woodbine: 414 Broadway, 3rd Floor, Manhattan

“Baravalle and Sholette, writier of , have decades of experience organizing in and with autonomous art spaces, critiquing the sites of art’s incorporation into the dominant orders of accumulation, and tracking modes of collective creative production that might signal other modes of creativity.”

📐 Terence Tao: Six Math Essentials, in conversation with Janna Levin
7pm | : 159 Pioneer St, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“Widely regarded as the world’s greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art—a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality.” Hosted by .

🎹 DURATIONS: An Evening with Terre Thaemlitz [Live Piano] + Conversation with Ciarán Finlayson
7pm | Public Records: 233 Butler St, Brooklyn | $42.23 | 21+

item.title: [field notes nyc] things to do in new york: nov 2 - 8
item.description: Indonesian Film Festival, Brooklyn Folk Festival and a celebration of sonnets
item.dc:creator: field notes nyc | Danielle
item.content:encoded:
Monday, November 2

🧵 Fabric of Resilience: Textile Afterlives of Connected Seas
2—5pm workshop; 6pm discussion | Onassis ONX: 390 Broadway, 4th Fl, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“Fabric of Resilience is an evolving collective installation exploring how fabrics carry memories of people and places, and how our relationships with the sea connect us through histories of migration, environmental change, and collective resilience. Bring your fabrics or work with existing fabrics to contribute to a collective textile landscape.” Discussion on Connected Seas: Environmental Histories, Psychogeography, and Architectures of Resilience.

👔 Suitable: The Sartorial Revolution and the Fashioning of Modern Men
5:30pm | The Museum at FIT: 227 W 27th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“Two hundred and fifty years after the American Revolution, historian and costume designer Dr. Chloe Chapin traces the evolution of modern men’s suits to answer big questions about fashion.”

🎞️ KASAT MATA / MACROSCOPIC: IFFest NY 2026 Pre-Event
7pm | Selva: 1329 Willoughby Ave, Brooklyn

“To kick off Indonesian Film Festival New York 2026, come join us a night of documentary shorts, either by Indonesian diasporic filmmakers or about the Indonesian diaspora.”

Tuesday, November 3

🍳 Counter Culture: New York City’s Greatest Diners and Luncheonettes
6pm | Village Preservation: 232 E 11th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“Join us as photographers James T. and Karla L. Murray speak about their most recent book, Counter Culture, and some of our neighborhoods’ and New York’s most iconic lunch spots such as B&H Dairy and Veselka. These street-level independent businesses, often family-owned, have been anchors in the community across generations. But in recent years, gentrification has forced many of the businesses to close their doors at an alarming rate.”

📷 The Naomi Rosenblum ICP Talks Photographer Lecture Series with Pierpaolo Mittica and Adam Higginbotham
6:30—8pm | ICP Library: 84 Ludlow St, Manhattan | $5+

Environmental photographer Pierpaolo Mittica (known for his Chernobyl work) in conversation with Adam Higginbotham, author of Midnight in Chernobyl and Challenger, moderated by ICP’s Erin Barnett.

🧪 The Museum as Test Bed: Ann Neumann, Building for Ideas That Don’t Exist Yet
7pm | The National Arts Club: 15 Gramercy Park South, Manhattan | Free

“What if a museum worked less like a warehouse for finished objects and more like a lab where the experiment is still running?”Ann Neumann, Director of Galleries and Exhibitions at MIT Museum, on the museum as infrastructure for public experimentation, including interactive projects on CRISPR, machine learning, and sensory neuroscience.

Wednesday, November 4

🏺 ISAW Exhibition Lecture: Cursing, Curing, Creating: The Culture of Magic in Ancient Egypt
5:30—6:30pm | Institute for the Study of the Ancient World (ISAW): 15 E 84th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

Egyptologist Foy Scalf (University of Chicago) on how ancient Egyptians used spells, amulets, and ritual to heal, protect, and curse. Given with ISAW’s exhibition Cursed! The Power of Magic in the Ancient World.

📜 A Celebration of the Sonnet, with Phillis Levin and special guests
6pm | The New York Society Library: 53 E 79th St, Manhattan | $15

“This year marks the 25th anniversary of the landmark The Penguin Book of the Sonnet: 500 Years of a Classic Tradition in English. Join its anthologist, poet Phillis Levin, along with Jonathan Galassi, Shane McCrae, Diane Mehta, Jason Schneiderman, and Tom Sleigh for an evening celebrating one of poetry's most enduring lyric forms”

🌾 Punjab: A Changing Landscape
7—9pm | Boyfriend Co-op: 1157 Myrtle Ave, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“A gathering for a conversation about the past, present, and future of Punjab’s land, rivers, and forests, facilitated by Puneet Singh.”

Subscribe now

Thursday, November 5

🌳 A Tree That Raised You: Short Film Screening and Documentary Writing Workshop
5:30—8pm | Field Meridians: 1136 President St, Brooklyn | $10 donation

“Short film screening and writing workshop by director . As the olive harvest season unfolds in Palestine, we’ll gather to watch Where the Wind Blows, a short documentary by Hana Elias following her family’s first olive harvest together as they reconnect with an ancestral tree and the stories that emerge from it.”

🎞️ Reel to Real: Brooklyn and Beyond: An Evening of Short Film & Conversation
6—8pm | Library for Arts & Culture: 10 Lafayette Ave, 2nd Fl, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

An evening of short film highlighting the work of multidisciplinary artist Jordan Blake. Post-screening Q&A with Blake and collaborator CJ Hart, moderated by Chyna Cassell. Blake is a Lagos-born, Brooklyn-based artist whose work centers Black beauty, masculinity, and style.

📓 Sketching & Bookbinding Workshop
6—8pm | Liz’s Book Bar: 315 Smith St, Brooklyn | $53.49

Sketching, portrait-drawing, and bookbinding combined!

🐪 Carved in Stone, Carried Across Deserts: Migration, Cultural Exchange, and the Art of the Silk Road
6:30—8pm | Asia Society: 725 Park Ave, Manhattan | $30

“Join Asia Society for a compelling new book conversation on cross-cultural encounter, migration, and visual art featuring Dr. Jin Xu, Jane and Leopold Swergold Associate Professor of Chinese Art History at Columbia University, and Dr. Xiaohan Du, John H. Foster Assistant Curator of Pre-Modern Art at Asia Society Museum.”

🎶 House Party 2026
7—11pm | BKCM Seventh Ave: 58 Seventh Ave, Brooklyn | $350

“Every year, on a dark November night, more than 500 illustrious guests and musical artists gather in BKCM’s mansion for a night of revelry and music: the one and only House Party.” Brooklyn Conservatory of Music’s biggest fundraiser (supports music education and music therapy). 20+ acts across the building.

🍻 LIC History Night
8pm | LIC Bar: 45-58 Vernon Blvd, Queens

Friday, November 6

🖨️ Free Friday Nights at the Whitney: Collagraph Printing with Robert Blackburn Workshop
5—10pm (collagraph workshop 7—9pm) | Whitney Museum of American Art: 99 Gansevoort St, Manhattan

Read more

item.title: [field notes nyc] things to do in new york: oct 26 - nov 1
item.description: Halloween, Marathon Day and everything in between
item.dc:creator: field notes nyc | Danielle
item.content:encoded:
Monday, October 26

📚 Robert McCracken Peck, Travels on the Edge: A Naturalist’s Notes from the Back of Beyond
6pm | The New York Society Library: 53 E 79th St, Manhattan | $15

“For almost fifty years, Bob Peck has traveled the world as the official photographer, historian, and chronicler of scientific expeditions from the Academy of Natural Sciences of Philadelphia, America’s oldest natural history institution, now part of Drexel University.”

Tuesday, October 27

🥂 Deez Drinks Vol. 2: Publishing Party!
6—9pm | Monsieur: 86 E 4th St, Manhattan | $20

Join for a mixer for publishing & book people! “Our second party is all about publishing and the business of books — co-hosted by Frances Goldin agents Caroline Eisenmann and Jade Wong-Baxter. Whether you’re interested in working in publishing, want to meet other folks who already work in books (including agents, editors, scouts, booksellers, critics, and more), OR just love reading and talking about books, we'd love to get to know you."

🧩 A New York Times Games Night to celebrate the release of Connections, the Book!
8pm | 92NY: 1395 Lexington Ave (enter on 92nd St), Manhattan | $48+

“What makes great puzzles like Connections (edited by Wyna Liu), the Mini Crossword (Joel Fagliano), Wordle (Tracy Bennett), and Spelling Bee (Sam Ezersky) impossible to put down? How does Wyna craft her famously tricky Connections puzzles — and can she stump her fellow editors?”

Wednesday, October 28

🇵🇭 The Anti-Inevitable: Kwentuhan On Filipino Folklore For Freedom
6—8pm | Library for Arts & Culture: 10 Lafayette Ave, 2nd Fl, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“For Filipino American History Month, we’ll explore Filipino folklore as a source of resistance and a powerful force in art making through an anti-imperialist lens.”

🎙️ Live Podcast Taping: “Locating Girlhood”
6—8pm | American Folk Art Museum: 2 Lincoln Square, Manhattan | $17.88

“Person Place Thing is an interview show built around the idea that people are often most engaging when they talk not directly about themselves, but about something they care deeply about. For this episode, curator Emelie Gevalt will discuss three exceptional works of girlhood art currently on view in detail.”

🎃 Pumpkitecture! Architectural Pumpkin Carving Competition
6—8:30pm | Center for Architecture: 536 LaGuardia Pl, Manhattan | $15

“Come witness architects live-carve extraordinary structures and vote for the People’s Pumpkin. We're asking carvers to create intricate and proportioned interior residential spaces.”

📖 Anand Giridharadas Discusses Man in the Mirror with Tara Westover
7—8:30pm | Central Library: 10 Grand Army Plaza, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“BPL Presents welcomes acclaimed journalist , who discusses Man in the Mirror, a groundbreaking feat of reporting on a tragic encounter in a New York subway car that held up a mirror to a troubled and divided nation.”

🎩 Houdini Among the Villagers
6—7:30pm | Church of the Village: 201 W 13th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“On this panel we’ll talk about Houdini’s rise to fame in New York, including the East Village, while learning wild facts about his life, his place in the history of stage magic alongside other luminaries and – in honor of the 100th anniversary of his death – Houdini’s meandering detour into the strange worlds of ghosts and Spiritualism.”

Subscribe now

Thursday, October 29

🎨 Walter Annenberg Lecture: Alex Da Corte
6:30pm | Whitney Museum of American Art: 99 Gansevoort St, Manhattan | $20

“Alex Da Corte is a Venezuelan-American artist inspired by Pop Art and Surrealism and informed by American cultural references. He is the co-curator of Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, which presents a retrospective of Lichtenstein in the contemporary context of accelerated production and circulation of images. For this Walter Annenberg Lecture, Alex Da Corte presents a talk about his engagement with Lichtenstein, combining his experiences as an artist and curator.”

🎭 Halloween Costume Contest
7—9pm | New Museum Lobby: 235 Bowery, Manhattan | Free

“Show off your Halloween spirit at the New Museum! Costumes will be judged in the Museum Lobby and the most devious (or playful) look will win a prize.”

🎬 Stanley Kubrick: A Life in Cinema
7pm—11:59pm | Nine Orchard: 9 Orchard St, Manhattan | $75+

With Criterion and TCM, join us for a very special panel discussion about Kubrick’s work and vision—followed by a pre-Halloween soirée. Panel with Matthew Modine, Vincent D’Onofrio, Lisa Leone, Josh Safdie, and Katharina Kubrick, moderated by TCM’s Ben Mankiewicz.

📚 Motherdom: A talk and conversation with Alex Bollen

7:30pm | Topos Too: 5922 Myrtle Ave, Queens | Free

“In what The New Yorker calls an “irascible, informative” book, draws on memoir, history, and science to examine the shaky evidence behind so much of today’s parenting advice and the shifting, impossible standards that leave mothers blamed whatever they do.”

Friday, October 30

📖 Adrift in the South: China’s Migrant Literature
6:30—8pm | Asia Society: 725 Park Ave, Manhattan | $30

“Join us for a lively conversation on the rise of China’s migrant worker literature, bringing the voices and lived experiences of the country’s vast internal migrant population into the literary mainstream.” A book talk with author Xiao Hai and translator Tony Hao, moderated by Alec Ash.

🦇 Nosferatu Meets Incarnate Jazz
7—10:30pm | Church of the Incarnation: 209 Madison Ave, Manhattan | $25+ $

Emerging from the shadows: an evening of electrifying jazz paired with the chilling nightmare of Nosferatu

🕯️ Hereafter Hours
6pm onwards | The Green-Wood Cemetery: 500 25th St, Brooklyn | $45

“As the veil grows thin and the gates close to the public, step into a side of Green-Wood few ever experience: after dark. Wander past monuments and mausoleums illuminated against the night sky while your guide brings to life the tales of some of our most fascinating permanent residents. The night ends with rare access inside the Catacombs, a space rarely opened to the public.”

Saturday, October 31

📷 ICP Photobook Club: Japanese Women Photographers x Art+Feminism Wikipedia Edit-a-Thon
11am—1pm | ICP Library: 84 Ludlow St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“Connect with fellow photobook enthusiasts, explore ICP’s library, and browse photobooks by Japanese women photographers exhibited in I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now, then edit the Wikipedia pages of the photographers featured in the exhibition.”

🍺 500 Beers of Solitude
8:30pm onwards | 100 Freeman St: Greenpoint, Brooklyn | $45 for drinks all night

“we’re throwing a party that starts in total silence for the fifth year running. nobody talks until 500 drinks have been consumed. until then we do cute quiet things together: crosswords, silent dancing, etc. the moment the last drink goes down, we turn into a normal, beautiful, feral, noisy party with big halloween energy.”

🖼️ Mildred Thompson Panel Discussion | Galerie Lelong: Dialogues
1—2pm | Galerie Lelong: 528 W 26th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“Galerie Lelong is proud to host a panel discussion about Mildred Thompson’s practice and role as a groundbreaking abstractionist on the occasion of the exhibition Cosmos Calling.”

👻 53rd Annual Village Halloween Parade
7pm | Sixth Avenue: Canal St to 15th St, Manhattan | Free

“Please come be with the spirits as we dance through our Village on the night when the veil between worlds is the thinnest! Everyone is invited to watch. All in costume are welcome to join in.”

🕯️ Philosophy at the Museum: Medieval Art at The Met Cloisters
2—4pm | The Met Cloisters: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, Manhattan | $9

“We will go from birth and ultimate beginnings, through life and purpose, to death and scary ends. Surrounded by the Age of Faith, we will conceptualize our own time in this world versus a time before and after us– inquiring into what it means to die in this world and continue unto the next. Through Gothic chapels and Unicorn tapestries, we will consider St. Augustine of Hippo’s view on the many deaths and ask: Is death the ultimate end? And, How does our life affect our death?”

Sunday, November 1

🏃 TCS New York City Marathon (50th edition)
One of the best days of the year!!!

💀 Day of the Dead 2026
4—6pm | Kaufman Courtyard, Museum of the Moving Image: 36-01 35 Ave, Queens | Free

“Celebrate a vibrant and authentic Day of the Dead at Museum of the Moving Image with a performance of Aztec Mexica dance, fun digital media activities for kids and families, music from the Indigenous dance troupe Yayauhki Tezcatlipoka, and the Mexican Folkloric Ballet of New York.”

make plans with a friend!

Share

Coming up soon…

  • Criterion Presents The Craft of Acting: Léa Seydoux (Nov 9, $25)

  • The Library After Hours: Friday the 13th Edition (Nov 13, by donation)

item.description: Pumpkins on Governors Island, annual Halloween Book Crawl and an all-night poetry reading
item.dc:creator: field notes nyc | Danielle
item.content:encoded:
13 days until the sun sets at 5pm… read my sauna guide if you’re looking for somewhere warm to hide.

Monday, October 19

🧘 McGolrick Meditation: Mindful Mondays with Bea Wolert
6—6:30pm | McGolrick Park: Monitor St between Driggs & Nassau Aves, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“Join Bea Wolert for weekly outdoor mindfulness sessions that combine breathwork, mindful walking, and simple creative practices like visualization, nature-based connection activities, sound mapping and intuitive drawing to ground the body, quiet the mind, and open creative awareness.”

🎬 Criterion Presents Adventures in Moviegoing with Isaac Mizrahi
7:30pm | Redstone Theater, Museum of the Moving Image: 36-01 35 Ave, Queens | $25

“Mizrahi joins Criterion’s Peter Becker for a live conversation about the films that have inspired his life and work.”

Tuesday, October 20

📚 Combat Breathing x Study Session with Joy James
6—8:30pm | Wendy’s Subway: 379 Bushwick Ave, Brooklyn | $25–75 sliding scale

“What drives us into rebellion towards the unknown, and what keeps us unknowingly paralysed from rebelling? In this study session, we will think collectively through categories developed in Joy James’s writing and political analysis, particularly the captive maternal, revolutionary love, rebellion, and the political “codes” through which societies and movements reproduce themselves”

🎭 Living the Avant Garde
6—7:30pm | Phyllis Harriman Mason Gallery: 215 W 57th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“Join us for a panel discussion organized in conjunction with the publication of The Art of Living in Avant-Garde Paris: Ethics and Self-Making in Dada, Simultanism, and Surrealism."

🎨 Everything I Wish I Learned in Design School (But Only Found Out Later) with Rich Tu
6:30—8pm | ARC*E-02 Lecture Hall, Pratt Institute: 200 Willoughby Ave, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

Rich Tu is an award-winning creative, illustrator and designer based in New York City.

Subscribe now

Wednesday, October 21

🧵 Embroidery as Memory w/ Nicole Montgomery
6—8:30pm | Elizabeth Catlett Art Space & Printmaking Studio: 320 W 37th St, Manhattan | $55.20

“This embroidery workshop is for participants to build an understanding of basic stitches while exploring the role of hand-sewing in history.”

🧛 Asian Feminist Horror Panel: Featuring NEEDLEMOUTH
8—10pm | The Twisted Spine: 306 Grand St, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“Join us for a special evening as we celebrate Asian Feminism in Horror! Celebrating ’s new novel NEEDLEMOUTH, with Catherine Dang, and ; moderated by Chandra Claypool.”

📚 2026 Louis Auchincloss Prize: Colson Whitehead
6:30pm | Museum of the City of New York: 1220 Fifth Ave, Manhattan | $35

“Celebrate two-time Pulitzer Prize–winning author Colson Whitehead whose novels and essays have long used New York City as a lens for examining history, identity, and American life.”

📚 Susan Orlean with John Wilson: Joyride — Paperback Launch
7:30pm | Buttenwieser Hall, 92NY: 1395 Lexington Ave, Manhattan | $30+ streaming from $25

“The beloved New Yorker writer and bestselling author of The Orchid Thief and The Library Book, , joins documentary filmmaker John Wilson for the paperback launch of Joyride: Orleans’ funny, restless, big-hearted memoir about a life spent chasing stories.”

🔊 Unsound New York (through 10/23)
7:30pm | Alice Tully Hall: 1941 Broadway, Manhattan | Sliding scale

Opening night of Unsound New York, a Kraków-born festival billed as a “sonic tour of unpredictable ingenuity” that blurs genre and pushes the boundaries of the aural avant-garde.

Thursday, October 22

🎧 Look & Feel: Exploring the Relationship Between Sound and Design
6:30—9pm | Index Greenpoint: 698 Manhattan Ave, Floors 2 & 3, Brooklyn | $10

“An experiment and gathering exploring the reciprocal relationship between sound and design. ​Join us for an evening of dancing and conversation as visual designers plug in their USBs, sharing sounds in a b2b setting.” Hosted by .

🪩 School Nite: Isabella Lovestory, B0YG1RL, ali rq (DJ)
7—11pm | MoMA PS1: 22-25 Jackson Ave, Queens | $17.08+

School Nite is MoMA PS1’s new, after-hours music series amplifying the next generation of sound.

📸 Bronx Documentary Center’s 15th Anniversary Benefit
6—9pm | Bronx Documentary Center: 614 Courtlandt Ave, Bronx | $15 suggested donation

“Join us for a 15th birthday celebration! This fundraiser event will support all of the BDC’s work and programming including the Youth Photo League, the Senior Photo League, the Film Fellows program, the Latin American Foto Festival, a roster of world-class exhibitions, free public events, and much more.”

Friday, October 23

🎬 FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO – THE AFTERMATH
Oct. 23–29 | Village East by Angelika: 181 Second Ave, Manhattan | $21.19

“The Trinity bomb story Oppenheimer left out. This award-winning doc follows the New Mexico families sickened by fallout from the first atomic bomb test, and their 80-year fight for justice.”

field trip alert!!!! join me this tuesday evening 10/13 at La Plaza Cultural in the East Village for chess and sauna 🌀

CUL DE SAC is a nonprofit bringing outdoor community saunas to new york. i’ve seen them grow so much in the last year, and am excited to partner with them as they launch their fundraiser for a winter residency.

i’ll be hosting a sauna-side chat + Q&A with the organizers at 7pm to hear more about how they started CDS and the mission behind it, so if you want to catch that, i’d suggest booking a time slot before or after! tickets are $25 for sauna + chess, and $15 for chess only. feel free to byo food.

7pm | Guggenheim: 1071 Fifth Ave, Manhattan | $15—65

Studios’ acclaimed comic, The Many Deaths of Laila Starr by Ram V. and Filipe Andrade, into a vivid and transporting tale for the operatic stage by composer Kamala Sankaram and librettist Minita Gandhi. 7pm | The Center for Fiction: 15 Lafayette Ave, Brooklyn | $30.68

“Join us as we celebrate the 25th anniversary of ’s groundbreaking debut novel, Edinburgh, a piercing coming-of-age story that grapples with the process of growing through, around, and beyond abuse. 📷 Boardwalk Studies
12—3pm | Luna Park: 1000 Surf Ave, Brooklyn (Coney Island) | $35

“A photowalk through the Coney Island boardwalk, framing everyday stories hiding in plain sight.”

💃 Moving Body – Moving Image
12—6pm | David Rubenstein Atrium: 1887 Broadway, Manhattan | Free first-come, first-served

A biennial movement film festival that explores creative movement and the immigrant experience. See the full schedule here!

🖼️ Points of View: 100 Connections to Art—A Conversation with Met Authors

“What do you see when you look at art? Join Met staff as they share their thought-provoking and surprising answers to this question and discuss a range of objects from famous highlights to little-known gems.”

item.title: Six saunas to escape the New York cold
item.description: Winter is coming... bring a swimsuit.
item.dc:creator: field notes nyc | Danielle
item.content:encoded:
The sauna is one of the few safe spaces to hide from the seasonal despair that is sunset by 5pm. I’m a late convert — I didn’t always understand the appeal of saunas. Being stuck in a hot, claustrophobic box with strangers, in a swimsuit, used to sound like a nightmare to me. A switch flipped in my late 20s. Perhaps it’s because I married someone with three sauna hats or because the hours spent shrimped over my laptop are catching up to me. Either way, here are my opinion on six saunas around the city.

Russian and Turkish Baths

Open since 1892 in the East Village, the Russian and Turkish Baths feels like you’re descending into a submarine in the basement of a townhouse. This isn’t going to be the most tranquil spa experience. People are constantly streaming between the saunas or perching on the tiled benches that line the baths. An old man may be handing out grapes. It’s a spa with extremes — possibly the hottest banya I’ve visited and a sickeningly cold, cold plunge. If you prefer something milder, join the smokers on the outdoor patio. This is an institution with years of lore. The baths are run on alternate weeks by two different owners, so if you become a regular, let me know if you’re a “David” or “Boris” week type of gal.

CUL DE SAC

A new addition to the sauna scene, CUL DE SAC is a collective with a mission to bring people together through wellness. They’ve been hosting sauna pop-ups throughout New York, showing up at community gardens and festivals. I visited their residency at La Plaza Cultural in the East Village, where they have two wood-burning plexiglass saunas. While saunaing, I could hear the chattering of sparrows and friend groups alike, and see the steam rising into the sky. I also liked the jarring feeling of being thrown into the elements when you step out of the sauna. The pop-up reminds me of the term “site specificity” in art because of the way they’ve integrated with the garden. There’s a stone amphitheater for laying out your towel to bask in the sun and music. They have a couple of cold plunges, and they’re meticulous about keeping them clean (a team member comes by after each plunge with a little fishing net). They just announced a fundraising campaign for a winter residency at Domino Square, and I’m co-hosting an event with them this Tuesday (Oct 13) — come check it out!

Bathhouse (Williamsburg)

I had written off Bathhouse as overrated, but after visiting, I have to say it’s justly rated. I went on a sunny Friday in late September, and maybe it was beginner’s luck, but the rooftop pool wasn’t too crowded. It felt like I was in a beautiful fever dream, sipping a spritz by the pool and taking in the Manhattan skyline. The pass is valid for the day, so if you’re also looking to maximize your ROI, get ready to hunker down until the evening. I gave the aufguss ceremony a try — it’s theatrical, definitely sauna and a show, but I did enjoy being fanned by the warm mandarin-scented wind. Rockwell Group designed the bathing space to make guests “feel as though they’ve discovered a slightly futuristic ruin from an ancient civilization,” and it largely delivers. The one oddity is a neon sign straight out of the “live laugh love” aesthetic.

Mermaid Spa

Mermaid Spa is on the outskirts of the aptly named Seagate, a Brooklyn neighborhood teetering on the edge of the Atlantic Ocean. A winter’s day out at Mermaid Spa is a trip. There was some uncertainty at the beginning of the experience (how did I end up here?), but soon the hours melted away as I cycled between the saunas and the pools. Suddenly it was dusk, and I was ejected onto the blue, barren streets. I waited fifteen minutes for a bus that never materialized, and ultimately shelled out for a taxi instead of making the brutal 45min trek to the Q. Was it worth it?? Yes, but make the trek before it gets too cold out. Mermaid Spa is roomy, with a dining and hangout area, so order beer and borscht, and bring some cards. The atmosphere is convivial — expect to share the space with families and middle-aged friend groups.

King Spa

The perfect day out in New Jersey: a spa day followed by Korean food, from samyetang and sundubu to bingsu. It’s the only spa I’ve been to where they have a freezer filled with assorted ice creams. I stumbled into a sauna that is heated to 280°F, and they gave us burlap sacks to shield us from the heat. After that intense experience, I returned to the healing room where there’s an adjustable heating screen that you can position anywhere on your body. At King Spa, there is ample space for lounging and hanging out. Play chess or checkers, or bring a book. Yes, bath-goers are required to be fully nude in the washing and bathing area, but fear not. After hours of relaxation in their signature baggy pink outfit, you’ll forget you even have a body. To secure a coveted spot on the complimentary shuttle, get to the K-town Dunkin’ Donuts bright and early because there are only about ten seats.

World Spa

There’s a fortress for relaxation in the middle of south Brooklyn. In contrast to the minimalist, industrial aesthetic of Bathhouse, World Spa is like Disneyland. I suspended my disbelief and tried out each of the various baths and saunas, traversing between the Moroccan hammam and the onsen in front of a glowing Mount Fuji. Between the saunas is a large restaurant area. I took a peek at the menu, and yes, you can order oysters, caviar and truffles. Attractions aside, my favorite spot is the infrared room with wooden seats that curve to support your reclined body. It’s a calming oasis amid the stimulation. Since you’re already in the area, go try out one of the Albanian restaurants in the neighborhood — we went to Si n’shpi and it was excellent.

And that’s not even half of it. This being New York, there’s a way to sweat for every taste and budget. Unfortunately, the most common is overheating in your coat on the subway.

Tell me about your favorite sauna or spa!

item.title: [field notes nyc] things to do in new york: oct 5 - 11
item.description: Throw away your smartphone, speed in design and a night with David Byrne
item.dc:creator: field notes nyc | Danielle
item.content:encoded:
Monday, Oct 5

📵 August Lamm + Catherine Shannon: You Don’t Need a Smartphone
7pm | Strand Book Store: 828 Broadway, Manhattan | $13.61+

“A book release event with writer and visual artist discussing her new book, “a revelatory manifesto” chronicling her journey from social media influencer to smartphone-free living — including downgrading to a dumb phone, navigating without GPS, and meeting people offline.” In conversation with .

Tuesday, Oct 6

📚 David Byrne on ‘Sleeping Beauties’
7pm | Riverside Church: 490 Riverside Dr, Manhattan | $40–$50 (incl. book)

“From incomparable creative force David Byrne, a brilliant and inspiring reckoning with how breakthroughs across the arts and sciences get forgotten, and how they get rediscovered.”

🪩 After Hours: Wanderlust
7–10pm | MoMA: 11 West 53 St, Manhattan | $30

“Join us for a night out at MoMA featuring art, performances, live music, and more. Leave traditional notions of travel behind, and experience an expansive idea of wanderlust—inspired by the energy of club culture and artistic collaboration.” Lineup includes a hands-on workshop, an L’Rain performance, an immersive fashion show, and a closing DJ set. Featuring .

🧖 Readings & Sauna at La Plaza Cultural
Sauna 5–8pm, readings 6–7:30pm | La Plaza Cultural: 137 Avenue C, Manhattan | $25

“Readings. Guitars. Sauna. Celestial minds. Steaming bodies. Byo swimsuit.” Hosted by William Kim and Cul de Sac, a community-centered, volunteer-run nonprofit — all profits go to sustain the project. The garden is open to all for readings, but RSVP for sauna slots.

🔌 Creative Technology Show and Tell
7–8:30pm | Index Chinatown: 120 Walker St 3rd Floor, Manhattan | $15
“A cozy, low-stakes gathering where artists and makers talk about their finished or in progress creative coding & physical computing work for 4-minutes each, to help demystify creative coding and physical computing, and connect over fun ideas and good snacks.”

submit an event!

Wednesday, Oct 7

🎨 Art Book Night
6:30–8:30pm | Finback Brewery: 545 President St, Brooklyn | Free

“Bring your favorite art book and come yap about It with some lovely strangers🗣️ Here’s how it works: → Bring an art book (any kind — photography, painting, cooking, design, zines, whatever floats your boat) to show off and browse others → Get crafty at our collage station — magazines, scissors, and glue provided so you can design your own imaginary art book cover.”

📸 MORE CAMERAS THAN PEOPLE
7pm | Earth: 49 Orchard St, Manhattan

“There are ~35 billion cameras in the world today, counting consumer devices alone... Jamieson Webster and will conduct a live mini-session of psychoanalysis exploring this question, followed by a discussion with .”

🏃 Fresh Dialogue~The Communication of Speed
6–7:30pm | Museum of Arts and Design: 2 Columbus Circle, Manhattan | $11.50+

“AIGA NY and the Museum of Arts and Design invite you to join artist and designer Julian Alexander, co-founder of Doubleday & Cartwright, Christopher Isenberg, and fine artist Simi Mahtani, for an invigorating conversation about design for sport. Both fields have shared tenets and goals that are an integral part of shaping our future.” Moderated by Anthony Harrison.

🖼️ Visionaries: Lucy Sante
6:30–8pm | New Museum Theater: 235 Bowery, Manhattan | $25

“The New Museum is proud to present the 2026 Visionaries event, honoring writer, critic, and artist Lucy Sante. For over three decades, Sante has written on photography, history, music, and her own life, affecting our understanding of the cultural landscape of New York City.”

📖 Emily Wilson presents Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea
7–8:30pm | Old First Reformed Church: 126 7th Ave, Brooklyn | $27.24

“Emily Wilson, renowned translator of Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey, presents Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea in Brooklyn... drawing on twenty years of scholarship and teaching, Wilson explores the difficult choices that translators must make, the pleasures of finding new solutions to old problems.”

Thursday, Oct 8

🌹 Garden Variety Joint Benefit
6-10pm| Elizabeth Street Garden: Elizabeth St, Manhattan | $75+

“One magical night, two great causes” — a benefit for Elizabeth Street Garden with Rosebuds Reading Collective. Admission includes open bar, food, and “Roses” (carnival currency for activities throughout the evening). 100% of proceeds benefit Elizabeth Street Garden Inc.

📚 Offsite: Banned Books Week Panel: Protect the Freedom to Read!
6–7pm | Brooklyn Public Library – Brooklyn Heights Branch: 286 Cadman Plaza West, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

A panel on fighting book bans and supporting banned authors in NYC, featuring NYCLU Executive Director Donna Lieberman, school library media specialist Karissa O’Reilly, authors Dr. Sonja Cherry-Paul and Rhonda Roumani, and PEN America’s Philomena Polefrone.

🛸 Brooklyn SciFi Film Festival at Nighthawk Cinema
7–9:30pm | Nitehawk Cinema Prospect Park: 188 Prospect Park West, Brooklyn | $15.18+

“12 award-nominated sci-fi short films from around the world” screen at this jury selections event, followed by award announcements and an after-party at Trees Lounge.

🔮 Practical Magic
7pm | Pier 57: 25 11th Ave, Manhattan | Free (RSVP)

“For two sisters from a family of witches, falling in love is the trickiest spell of all.” Sally and Gillian Owens give themselves a crash course in hard magic after Gillian’s vicious boyfriend dies unexpectedly — and unwittingly summon an evil spirit that threatens their family line.

Friday, Oct 9

🎬 The Downtown Festival (through Oct 18)
Multiple venues across Lower Manhattan | Varies by event

“THE DOWNTOWN FESTIVAL™ is a celebration of independent film, music, art, and culture held throughout Lower Manhattan each October. Featuring film premieres, anniversary screenings, live music performances, artist talks, and one-night-only events in storied cultural venues and underground spaces, the festival brings together emerging voices and established artists across generations and disciplines.” Founded by filmmaker Rebekah Sherman-Myntti as an artists-for-artists platform — worth a look at the full program for specific picks.

7pm | : 232 52nd St, Brooklyn | $25

“An evening devoted to nonsense in all its musical forms: songs, sounds, improvisations, wrong turns, and happy accidents. Where musicians take their cues from the audience, from each other, and occasionally from nowhere in particular.”

🎭 Shakespeare and Verdi’s Macbeth: Discussion and Performance
7—8pm | The Cooper Union: 7 East 7th St, Manhattan | Free

Louisa Proske, director of the Metropolitan Opera’s new production of Verdi’s Macbeth, and James Shapiro, the Public Theater’s Shakespeare Scholar in Residence, discuss parallels between the original text and Verdi’s opera. Includes performances from cast members alongside play excerpts.

Tuesday, September 29

🧵 Textile as Ancestral Memory: Film Screening & Panel Discussion
7—9pm | Oko Farms: 99 Scott Ave, Brooklyn | $25

“We invite you to a special screening of our travels to West Africa and Indonesia, where we had the privilege of meeting and learning from weavers, natural dyers, and farmers who are dedicated keepers of traditional textile practices.”

🎶 Cosmic Music: The Life, Art, and Transcendence of Alice Coltrane
7pm | Unnameable Books: 615 Vanderbilt Ave, Brooklyn

“ in conversation with for Cosmic Music: The Life, Art, and Transcendence of Alice Coltrane, in the backyard.”

🧶 Frogged Knit Club: One Year Anniversary
6—9pm | Rhodora Wine Bar: 197 Adelphi St, Brooklyn | Free

“Frogged Knit Club is back! Just in time for our one year anniversary. Join us back where it all began.”

Wednesday, September 30

💅 In Praise of Divas: Mariah Carey and Whitney Houston
7:30—8:30pm | Greenlight Bookstore: 686 Fulton St, Brooklyn | Free

Cultural critics Andrew Chan and Emily Lordi unite for an exploration of pop divas, fandom, and music history. Chan presents his work on the creative evolution, complicated biography, and legacy of Mariah Carey; Lordi launches her first major biography of Whitney Houston, drawing on access to the star’s innermost circle.

🎞️ The Material Is the Message
7:30pm | Titus Theater 1, MoMA: 11 West 53rd St, Manhattan | $14

“No camera? No problem. The material constraints of ultra-low-budget filmmaking have always required creative solutions. The works in this program rise to that challenge, casting the medium itself as a main character. Whether this involves painting a psychedelic riot of color onto the surface of a filmstrip—as in Peyote Queen and Alchemy Blues—or arming small children with safety pins to scratch away at its surface (Children Make Movies), the possibilities are endless.”

Subscribe now

Thursday, October 1

🎥 Fall of Freedom — Under Pressure: How to Document “Unprecedented Times”
7:30pm | UnionDocs: 352 Onderdonk Ave, Queens | $10

“How do documentary makers continue to work critically, responsibly, and safely in a rapidly shifting political landscape, and one that is increasingly threatening to those organizing and documenting on the ground? Presented as part of Fall of Freedom, this conversation brings together filmmakers and collaborators Rachel Lauren Mueller and Laura Poitras, with radio producer and Radiolab creator Jad Abumrad to consider the practical and ethical questions facing political documentary in the United States today.”

🕺 New York in the 1970s: When Music Saved the City
6:30—7:30pm | New York Historical: 170 Central Park West, Manhattan | $40

“Join us for a panel conversation and reception featuring some thrilling legends of the 1970s music scene, including Marky Ramone of the Ramones, Lenny Kaye of the Patti Smith Group, MC Sha-Rock of The Funky 4 +1, and Nicky Siano, a DJ who revolutionized disco at Studio 54 and The Gallery among other venues.”

Friday, October 2

🏮 Mid-Autumn Festival 2026 (through Sunday)
1—7pm | Gotham Park: 1 Rose St, Manhattan | Free

A three-day celebration of Mid-Autumn Festival featuring cultural programming, vendor experiences, and entertainment. Over a dozen Asian-owned food vendors and an arts and culture marketplace of Asian American makers and designers. Featuring family Mahjong instruction, Mooncake Play-Doh workshops, lantern-making, and a lantern parade.

🎸 Guitar Icons: Kingfish
7pm | The Metropolitan Museum of Art | $35+

“Grammy-winning, Billboard chart–topping guitarist Christone “Kingfish” Ingram bears the torch for a new era of blues, honoring the musical spirit of his Mississippi Delta upbringing while blurring the genre’s borders with funk, soul, hip-hop, pop, and jazz. Now, hear the blues like nowhere else as Kingfish and his all-star band—plus a few special guests— adventure through the genre’s cultural, historic, and artistic impact featuring a historical instrument from The Met collection.”

📚 Elizabeth Strout in Conversation
6:30pm | The National Arts Club: 15 Gramercy Park South, Manhattan | Free (RSVP required)

“In her most recent novel, Pulitzer Prize-winning author tells the story of a beloved teacher, Artie Dam, and a chance incident that sparks a powerful realization and change in his life. He looks out at the world - at himself and the people around him - and turns a question over and over in his mind: How is it that we know so little about one another, even those closest to us? With exquisite prose and profound insight, Strout’s new novel provides a poignant meditation on loneliness, friendship, parenthood, and the importance of truth in a capsizing world.”

🖼️ First Friday
12—8pm | Poster House: 119 W. 23rd St, Manhattan | Free

Free admission and extended hours, with rotating exhibitions and permanent collections through docent-led tours, workshops, film screenings, happy hour, and live music. Featuring a cyanotype and collage workshop, paper arts workshop and more.

Saturday, October 3

🏚️ Build a Brownstone with Celebrate Bed Stuy!
10am—12pm | Artshack Annex: 1127 Bedford Ave, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“Join Artshack X Celebrate Bed Stuy to “Build a Brownstone” facade out of clay! This class is free to the community. Before the hands-on workshop begins, a teaching artist from Celebrate Bed Stuy will provide a historical foundation on the significance of Juneteenth and the legacy of the brownstones in Bed-Stuy. By highlighting three historic neighborhood brownstones, participants will learn about there architectural style and cultural importance grounding the “Build a Brownstone” experience.”

🚢 Poetry on the River: A Poets House Benefit with Rickey Laurentiis, Ariana Reines, and Tracy K. Smith
4:45—7pm | Brookfield Place Ferry Terminal, Manhattan | $175

“Please join us for Poetry on the River: A Poets House Benefit, a poetry reading taking place on a sunset ferry cruise down the Hudson River with acclaimed poets Rickey Laurentiis, , and . After the reading, enjoy some light hors d’oeuvres and drinks in the company of the poets themselves and other poetry-lovers.”

📷 Make Along: Make a Pinhole Polaroid Camera from a Beer or Soda Can!
6—9pm | NYCResistor: 87 3rd Ave, 4th floor, Brooklyn | $28.52

“Together we will make pinhole cameras from two cans. Cans will be provided or you can bring your own favorite cans.”

Sunday, October 4

🎪 Greenpoint StoopFest
1—5pm, closing party 5—7pm | Lorimer St hub (between Nassau & Norman St), Greenpoint, Brooklyn | Free

“Greenpoint StoopFest is a first-of-its-kind neighborhood festival. Stoops are where people really connect, and the day is designed to make that happen – and to celebrate the history and communities that make Greenpoint what it is.”

🏛️ Crown Heights North Architectural History Tour
12—2pm | Grant Gore, Bedford & Dean, Brooklyn | Pay what you wish ($15 suggested)

“This tour will highlight the architecture and history of Crown Heights North. From the late 18th century to today, this neighborhood has had many differing groups call its streets home. The architecture represents urban growth, investment, disinvestment and reinvestment, highlighting these demographic and historic changes. Considered by many to hold some of Brooklyn’s finest late 19th and early 20th century architecture, we shall explore artistic movements and trends as realized in brick, terra cotta and stone, for residential, commercial and religious spaces.”

🖐️ Tactile Listening
10am—12pm | Pioneer Works: 159 Pioneer St, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“A treeline shivers. A stone shifts. Breath takes shape as voice to displace air. Sounds are also shapes to be known through feeling. This Tactile Listening workshop led by Ariana Martinez, Nour Yusoff, Anna RG, and the Sick Music Center shares ways of listening to, interpreting, and performing sound that move fluidly between hearing and touch. This is a hands-on workshop exploring sonic and tactile connections, moving outward from Ariana Martinez's installation, [river through wood with breath].”

🪡 Darn It! Mending Club at the Textile Arts Center
6—8:30pm | Textile Arts Center: 505 Carroll St, Brooklyn | $12.51

“Mending is a form of resistance! Lets celebrate fall, by pulling our knits out of hibernation and coming together at the Textile Arts Center where we can explore intervening our disposable outlook of fashion through the act of mending our precious textiles: forming relationships with our clothes, objects, and with each other. Monday, September 21

🍴Book Launch: Fundamentals of Flavor by Nik Sharma
6:30—8pm | POWERHOUSE Arena: 28 Adams St, Brooklyn | $5+

“Acclaimed cookbook author, America’s Test Kitchen Editor in Residence, and molecular biologist presents his latest work combining scientific knowledge with practical recipes. The book features 100 recipes exploring how fire, earth, air, and water enhance kitchen techniques and flavor.” In conversation with .

🎭 Opera Italiana is in the Air
6.30 - 8pm | Central Park: Naumburg Bandshell| Free

Mission is to make Italian opera accessible to everyone, with high-quality, informal, free open-air performances.

Tuesday, September 22

🐙 Science & Society: The Ocean Frontier
 8pm | : 159 Pioneer St, Brooklyn | Free (RSVP required)

“The ocean holds a key to our climate future—if we act wisely. In this episode of Science & Society, we delve into questions of industrializing the ocean, including deep sea mining and offshore renewable energy infrastructure, touching on scientific, social, and policy aspects.”

📚 Rong Xin Book Launch: On Flushing, Immigrants, and Beyond
6—8pm | initial research: 41 Wooster St #floor 2, Manhattan | By donation

The launch of Rong Xin, a publication that takes a shopping mall as a microcosm of Flushing, capturing its intricate details within.

🏙️ 2026 Mumford Lecture: Carlos Moreno on Proximity as a New Social Contract for Cities
6—7:30pm | Great Hall, Spitzer School of Architecture (Shepard Hall, CCNY), Manhattan | Free

“Please join us for the 2026 Mumford Lecture: From Crisis to Proximity: A New Social Contract for Cities, presented by Carlos Moreno. Today’s urban crises — climate disruption, rising inequalities, mobility pressure, housing shortages, and social fragmentation — lie at the heart of deteriorating well-being and quality of life. In a predominantly urban world, it is essential to pursue deep reflection and decisive action to transform this malaise through new urban approaches. Throughout history, proximity — the capacity for people to remain connected — has been a key lever for rebuilding social cohesion.”

Wednesday, September 23

📕 n+1 Issue 54 Reading and Celebration
7pm | n+1 office: 37 Greenpoint Ave #316, Brooklyn | $10

“Please join n+1 at our office in Greenpoint for reading and drinks in celebration of Issue 54: POWER PLAY!”

8pm | Signal: 175 Morgan Ave, Brooklyn | $22.85

“We Live in Public (2009, dir. Ondi Timoner) is the Sundance Grand Jury Prize-winning documentary about Josh Harris, the early internet pioneer behind Pseudo.com, the world’s first live-streaming platform. The film traces his rise, collapse, and eerie foresight into social media, surveillance, and life online.

6—7:30pm | Museum of Arts and Design: 2 Columbus Circle, Manhattan | $11.50+

“Where curatorial vision meets typography, motion, and print. Over 45 international short and feature length films. Curated in 9 programs, these stories appeal to a wide audience from film enthusiasts to avid cyclists and everyone in between. There will be a Q&A after each program.

6—8:30pm | Schimmel Center: 9 Spruce St, Manhattan | $10

Screening highlights from a new documentary series — WTC site rebuilding, new public/residential/cultural districts, infrastructure, equity, and climate resilience.

🧠 Does Expertise Matter?: Authority in the Age of Infinite Information
7—9pm | Index Chinatown: 120 Walker St 3rd Floor, Manhattan | $20

An interactive seminar exploring the concepts of expertise and intellectual authority, with reference to ongoing shifts in technology, politics, and education.

5:30—7pm | 1136 President St, Brooklyn | By donation

A lacto fermentation workshop facilitated by artist Adriana Gallo in which we will ferment seasonal fruits and vegetables from Battery Park Farm using a dry, vacuum sealing technique.

7—9pm | Brooklyn Museum, Rubin Pavilion: 200 Eastern Pkwy, Brooklyn | $30

Explore the worlds of designer Iris van Herpen in this installment of Art History Happy Hour, our lighthearted lecture series. Short talks from curator Matthew Yokobosky, mathematician Ingrid Daubechies, material science professor Deborah Berhanu, and art historian Lynn Gamwell, then a viewing of Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses.

4—11pm | Mercury Store: 131 8th St, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

6—10pm | Domino Square: 12 South 3rd St, Brooklyn | Free

6:30—7:30pm | Fraunces Tavern Museum, 2nd Floor: 54 Pearl St, Manhattan | $20

“Raise a glass to freedom and sing along to traditional songs from the colonial era, on authentic 18th-century instruments including a hammered dulcimer and a 1776 violin.
Anne and Ridley Enslow lead, in period dress, with a limberjack puppet and historical context before each piece.”

7pm | The National Arts Club: 15 Gramercy Park South, Manhattan | Free

“Grammy-nominated composer James Díaz presents a performance featuring his new album Espacio absoluto, centered on fictional spaces, unstable sonic environments, and perceptual transformation.”

🧵 Interior Textiles Today: A New York Perspective
6:30—8pm | Bob Fisch Hall, FIT: 227 West 27th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

“What does it actually take to build and sustain an interior textile practice in this city right now? Organized by New York Textile Month, FIT’s Surface Design program, and Textile Eye. Presentations from Saana Baker (Textile Eye), Lori Weitzner, and William Storms, followed by a moderated panel.”

6—8:30pm | Kaufmann Theater, American Museum of Natural History: 200 Central Park West, Manhattan | $15 / $12 members

“This after-hours program celebrates poetry and climate through readings by acclaimed poets Jane Hirshfield, Kimiko Hahn, and Brandon Kilbourne — followed by a guided writing exercise (no experience required) and a panel on how science, nature, and art come together to inspire change.”

7pm | The Center for Fiction: 15 Lafayette Ave, Brooklyn | $10+

“Lydia Mathis’s debut story collection, set in the American South, explores the desire, humor, and horror in the everyday lives of Black women and girls.” Launch conversation with on power imbalances, ambition, and female identity across girlhood and womanhood. Book signing follows; books sold separately.

7pm | Night Club 101: 101 Avenue A, Manhattan | price TBD need price

“ is back from summer vacation with a screening of the films of Haydée Caillot. Caillot was a collaborator of Eric Rohmer who acted in some of his films in addition to directing her own. Caillot’s films explore the themes of happenstance and love, always with a bit of humor and a tarot scene thrown in for good measure.”

🧠 Stavros Niarchos Foundation Brain Insight Lecture: Finding Meaning in Memories
6:30—7:45pm | Jerome L. Greene Science Center: 605 West 129th St, Manhattan | Free

“Memory is fundamental for our ability to learn, make decisions, and guide future behaviors. Columbia’s Zuckerman Institute lecture series. Daphna Shohamy on memory and decision-making, Ashok Litwin-Kumar on how bodily experience shapes memory in fruit flies, Q&A moderated by Isabel Low.”

🐉 Technology and Storytelling: Ken Liu and The Passing of the Dragon
6:30—7:30pm | Asia Society: 725 Park Ave, Manhattan | $30

“A thought-provoking evening with multi-award-winning speculative fiction author , for the release of his new collection, The Passing of the Dragon and Other Stories.”

📚 Malala Yousafzai + Charley Burlock: Finding My Way
Doors 6:30pm, event 7pm | The Strand Building, 6th Floor: 826 Broadway, Manhattan | $38.86

“Malala Yousafzai’s paperback memoir traces her path from high school loner to reckless college student to a young woman at peace with her past — exploring friendship, first love, and self-discovery.”

🎉 Carnival at the Museum: A Climate Fete
7—11pm, last entry 10pm | Rose Center for Earth and Space, AMNH: 200 Central Park West, Manhattan (enter at 81st St) | $30

“Grab a drink, savor Caribbean bites, dance in the Hall of the Universe, and explore climate action under the Blue Whale.” Live sets from Machel Montano plus dancehall/soca DJs, Lightning Lectures on climate, a panel on the sargassum crisis affecting Caribbean communities, Afro-Haitian and dancehall movement classes via Ailey Extension, and a local makers marketplace.

Thursday, September 17

⌨️ Shift Ctrl
7—8:30pm | Triple Canopy: 264 Canal St #3W, Manhattan | Free (RSVP required)

“Over the past decade, class conflict has erupted in the tech industry. While Silicon Valley executives curried favor with the Trump Administration, tech employees organized against, for example, contracts with the military and big oil, as well as for increased worker protections and, eventually, unions.” Authors Clarissa Redwine and (Against Tech Oligarchy) join artists Tega Brain and Sam Lavigne to discuss organizing tactics and leverage for white-collar tech workers.

🧠 Why We Create, and Don’t Create
6:30—9pm | Index Chinatown: 120 Walker St, 3rd Floor, Manhattan | $15

A conversation on the origins of creativity, why it matters, and what’s at stake as technology reshapes how we create. Wilson Brown (Creative Director, Antfood) and David “BBQ Dave” Sheinkopf (Co-Founder, Smooth Technology) in conversation.

🏙️ Building the Future of NYC
7—8:30pm | The Great Hall, Cooper Union: 7 East 7th St, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

City planning, from affordability to aesthetics and public space — creative professionals and policymakers on building equitable communities. Cooper Union alumni panel: City Council Member Shekar Krishnan, artist David Brooks, architect Savina Romanos; moderated by WNYC/Gothamist’s Liam Quigley.

submit an event

Friday, September 18

🌿 Book Launch: Tending the Vines by Ashia S. Ajani
7—9pm | POWERHOUSE Arena: 28 Adams St, Brooklyn (Dumbo) | $5+

“This standout creative nonfiction debut explores the lives and histories of plants considered nonnative or invasive as metaphors for the Black experience in America.” conversation with poet/journalist Irene Vázquez.

🎙️ Cabaret Conversations: Lindsay Mendez
7:30pm | Warburg Lounge, 92NY: 1395 Lexington Ave, Manhattan | $60+

“Broadway favorite Lindsay Mendez (Merrily We Roll Along, Wicked) joins cabaret expert Michael Kirk Lane for an intimate evening of conversation and music — the first-ever in-person edition of 92NY’s award-winning Cabaret Conversations series. Hear Mendez reflect on her life onstage, her artistic journey, and the experiences that have shaped her celebrated career. Accompanied by Yasuhiko Fukuoka on piano, she’ll also bring her extraordinary musical talent to this rare live appearance.”

✍️ Reading for Writers: Virginia Woolf’s “Street Haunting”
10:30am | Webster Library: 1465 York Ave, Manhattan | Free

“We’ll spend the morning with Virginia Woolf’s essay “Street Haunting: A London Adventure,” close reading it together and digging into the stylistic elements: how she builds an image, where a sentence turns, the small choices that make her prose do what it does.” Hosted by .

4—9pm | Green-Wood Cemetery: 500 25th St, Brooklyn | Free

Reimagine your textiles and clothes with new hand block printed patterns in this hands on workshop. Third year running from Cynthia Director Studio, part of New York Textile Month. 💿 Brooklyn Flea Record Fair at Smorgasburg
11am—6pm | Smorgasburg Williamsburg need address, Brooklyn | Free entry

👁️ EYE-CATCH! Fashion Show

“Join for our inaugural fashion show featuring wearable pieces by Jianing Zhao, Nathalie San Fratello, Tanner Kok, Lexi Fujita, and Dennis RedMoon Darkeem, winning stylists from the School’s EYE-CATCH! open call. Each stylist will showcase four looks inspired by the aesthetics and counter-aesthetics of the Attention Economy, brought to life by twenty models as our Dumbo Sanctuary transforms into a runway.”

3:30—8pm | Flux IV: 56-21 2nd St, Long Island City, Queens | Free with RSVP

“A public program examining urban water infrastructure as civic, social, and cultural framework — water as civic infrastructure and a catalyst for environmental resilience, public health, and community well-being.”.

10am—4pm | Old Stone House: 336 3rd St, Brooklyn (Park Slope) | Free

NYC’s only bicycle flea market where you can buy new and used bicycles, bicycle accessories, bicycle collectibles, clothing and other bicycle treasures.

The Strand celebrates 99 years of independent bookselling with 20% off in-store and online.

11:30am—4:30pm | Museum of the Moving Image: 36-01 35th Ave, Astoria, Queens | Free

“New Yorkers coexist with urban wildlife — coyotes in Central Park, whales and dolphins off the Rockaways, peregrine falcons on high-rises.” Panel with Mark Weckel (Gotham Coyote Project), Chris St. Lawrence (Gotham Whale), Mel Julien (NYC Plover Project), moderated by Nathan Hunter. 11am—4:30pm | Grace Rainey Rogers Auditorium, The Met Fifth Avenue: 1000 Fifth Ave, Manhattan | Free with RSVP

From clapping hands and tapping feet to beatboxing and whistling, the human body is a musical instrument. Musical Bodies examines how musical instruments, in turn, often draw their form and decoration from our bodies.

11am—6pm | Travers Park: 34th Ave, Jackson Heights, Queens | Free

Join a free clothing exchange! Come drop off your clean, ready-to-wear clothing and browse and take items that work for you — no cost for taking any number of items, no cost for dropping off. Part of Street Works Earth — the annual street-arts-and-climate-action festival at Travers Park.

📕 Artbook | D.A.P. Sample Sale
5—9pm | Rodeo: 1134 President St, Brooklyn | Free

“A sample sale of books pulled from the shelves of our NYC offices; all priced at $5, $10, $20, $40 and special high ticket items on deep discount.”

🌱 Eco Arts Festival 2026
11am—4pm | The Climate Imaginarium: 406A Comfort Rd, Governors Island | Suggested donation

A day of eco-inspired performances, installations, films and interactive workshops and activities that are free and open to the public, produced by Artichoke Dance Company. Workshops include an endangered aquatic animals installation, paper making, edible insects, and recycled fabric weaving, plus dance performances centered on environmental justice.

make plans w a friend!

August Recap

The late occurrence of Labor Day has thrown my month off kilter and it feels like we should be one week behind where we actually are. This summer I discovered that it’s really not so difficult to get to Jacob Riis and Fort Tilden beaches via the MTA (subway + the Q35 comes every 10 mins or so.) Compared with Coney Island or the Rockaways, Jacob Riis and Fort Tilden feel more like a beach getaway outside of the city. There are a couple of vendors near Jacob Riis — grabbing a soft serve is mandatory. The two beaches are also home to a variety of shore birds (shout out to the Piping Project for their conservation efforts), and there’s a host of didactic yet entertaining posters, made by kids, that line the boardwalk. One of the most satisfying things I’ve ever witnessed was a group of oystercatchers squawking and diving at some guy’s drone until he put it away 🤠.

Yes, I partook in line culture too. Lisbonata soft serves are a fun sweet treat and I’m impressed by the flavor combos they’re dropping every week. My favorite has been the Hojicha Sour Cherry but my humble opinion is to ask them to go light on the chocolate drizzle or honestly, skip it altogether because it overwhelms the other flavors. In the West Village, Myka and Birdies are frozen yogurt purveyors located on opposite sides of the street with parallel lines streaming out from each door… a setup to some joke about late stage capitalism. We started in the Myka line then jumped ship to Birdies because it seemed shorter. Was it worth it? Yes. We were wrapping up our evening so it wasn’t too bad waiting in line and enjoying the balmy night — if conditions had been more uncomfortable, it wouldn’t be something I’d be willing to wait more than 15 mins for.

On the last weekend of August, I finally went to see Oh Mary! with Meg Stalter and it was so camp and hilarious!! Sadly not on the 2-for-1 Broadway Week list of offerings.

Monday, September 7

🥁 J’Ouvert & West Indian American Day Carnival
J’Ouvert 6—11am, Carnival 11am—6pm | Eastern Parkway: Crown Heights, Brooklyn | Free

J’Ouvert originates from the French words “jour ouvert,” meaning daybreak or morning, and signals the start of Carnival. Steel band music dominates the early morning hours as participants “wining and chipping” precede the daytime carnival festivities — representatives of all Caribbean nations in vibrant costumes, with music and cultural performances. The city estimates roughly 1 million attendees along the Eastern Parkway route.

🍖 Chef Pickle BBQ Pop-Up x Farm.One
From 2pm | Farm.One: 625 Bergen St, Brooklyn
”Something for everyone since 2021. Join Chef Pickle for a new BBQ pop-up event over Labor Day Weekend! Woodfired Cajun wings, local oysters, grilled peach ice cream sandwiches, butter-bathed corn on the cob, crazy-style pickleslaw, and the hyper-seasonal veggie plate of your dreams sourced from Grow NYC Green Market.”

Tuesday, September 8

🎤 Brooklyn Poetry Slam
7pm | BRIC House: 647 Fulton St, Brooklyn | Free

“An evening of poetry and community co-founded by Mahogany L. Browne and Jive Poetic, featuring special guests and poets from across the city and beyond. The slam competition offers 5 slots and open mic provides 7 slots, names chosen randomly.”

🚶 Along the Creek: A Guided Exhibition and Walking Tour
5:30—7:30pm | ISCP: 1040 Metropolitan Ave, Brooklyn | Free

“Join Newtown Creek Alliance and ISCP for a guided walking tour presented in conjunction with the exhibition Hans Rosenstrom: Conspirare. The approximately 2.5-mile roundtrip route follows the industrial waterfront to Plank Road, where Gus Perry discusses the ecological and industrial histories of the creek.”

7pm | n+1 office: 37 Greenpoint Ave #316, Brooklyn | Free

“A celebration of Samuel Stein’s forthcoming book A Right to Housing? from Verso Books. Stein discusses the work with former n+1 coeditor and Pennsylvania state senator Nikil Saval.”

Wednesday, September 9

🎬 Summer Movies in the Park: The Namesake — 20th Anniversary Screening
 Q&A 7:30pm, film 8pm | Fort Greene Park, Central Lawn: Washington Park & DeKalb Ave, Brooklyn | Free

“Prospect Park Alliance, Fort Greene Park Conservancy, and Rooftop Films present a free outdoor movie series. This 121-minute film by Mira Nair follows the Ganguli family’s journey from Calcutta to New York, adapted from Jhumpa Lahiri’s novel, exploring how parents Ashoke and Ashima navigate cultural adaptation while their son Gogol struggles to balance heritage with personal identity.”

🏛️ Ground Zero Plus 25
7—9pm | The Great Hall at Cooper Union: 7 E 7th St, Manhattan | $24

“It has been 25 years since the terror attacks that destroyed the World Trade Center towers, killing more than 2,700 people and rending the landscape of Lower Manhattan. The rebuilding effort that followed began with an outpouring of proposals from the world’s most prominent architects—some mournful or pragmatic, others wildly speculative—before running aground in political acrimony.” Hosted by Review of Architecture and featuring .

📸 Sex, Clubs, Dissent: Visualising Queer Nightlife, with Amelia Abraham and Linda Simpson
6:30—8pm | ICP: 84 Ludlow St, Manhattan (Lower East Side) | $5+

“Journalist and editor Amelia Abraham converses with artist Linda Simpson to mark the publication of her latest editorial work, a vivid history of queer nightlife that examines how image-making has both fostered and jeopardized the formation of queer practices and subcultures — charting an expansive visual history through photography and film, exploring how photography intersects with pleasure, politics, and protest.”

Multiple Brooklyn venues: including Center for Fiction, Brooklyn Children’s Museum, MoCADA | Individual events free—$35; day passes $60/$100

Multi-day festival programming: panels on Caribbean music heritage (a Sister Nancy discussion), coastal justice, Caribbean culinary traditions and more. Featured speakers include Edwidge Danticat, Nicole Dennis-Benn, and .

Subscribe now

Thursday, September 10

🎬 Ridgewood Off-Kilter Film Festival (ROFF) (through Sunday)
Thu—Sun, Sep 10—13 | Various Ridgewood venues

A neighborhood-scale film festival screening shorts, docs, and features across multiple small Ridgewood venues over four nights. See link for full schedule.

📚 An Evening with Emma Cline
7—8pm | McNally Jackson Books at BKLYN STUDIOS: 1 Dekalb Ave, Brooklyn | $37 (includes book)

“Emma Cline discusses her forthcoming novel Switzy, a mesmerizing portrait of an aging man’s last pilgrimage. The narrative follows David, a retired executive on a winter journey involving stopovers in London, France, and Zurich, as his grasp on the present slips away, and the past rushes in.”

7—9pm | Maysles Documentary Center: 343 Lenox Ave/Malcolm X Blvd, Manhattan | $15 / $7 reduced

“Frederick Wiseman’s acclaimed 2015 documentary (190 minutes) immerses viewers in everyday life across Queens’ Jackson Heights neighborhood, “the most diverse neighborhood in the world.” The film follows activities at a Muslim school, Jewish center, LGBTQ+ gathering, City Council office, and Make the Road New York headquarters. In an extraordinary, rare New York appearance, internationally acclaimed couturier Guo Pei invites you into the magical realm of her creative universe. “Celebrating the label’s 70th anniversary, featuring Samara Joy (six-time GRAMMY winner from the Bronx) and Christian McBride (11-time GRAMMY winner). Mei Semones — an American indie rock musician who writes jazz-influenced songs in both English and Japanese — performs with collaborators aron!, Liana Flores, and John Roseboro, playing music from Getz/Gilberto, the classic collaborative album by João Gilberto and Stan Getz released on Verve in 1964.”

🥕 The Curious Lives of Vegetables: A Live Conversation with Ali Francis
6pm onwards | Farm To People: 1100 Flushing Ave, Brooklyn | $25+

“A book launch and live conversation with and Michael Ray Robinov of Farm to People, exploring vegetable history through botanical art, plus a live “Know Your Food” podcast recording covering biodiversity, regenerative farming, and extraordinary produce.”

🐮 Niú Lái (2026) Free Film Screening (multiple screenings this week)
Doors 5pm, film 7pm | : 4 Irving Ave, Brooklyn | Free

“Be the first to see the birth of a cult classic — Niú Lái / 牛来 (2026) is an animated movie from China about a cow stuck in an elaborate dream and has to learn how to be brave.”

🎤 Sing for Science: Kota the Friend & Kevin Quashie in Conversation
6:30–8pm | Poster House: 119 W 23rd St, Manhattan | $15

“Poster House collaborates with the podcast Sing for Science to host a conversation celebrating the final days of the “Act Black: Posters from Black American Stage & Screen” exhibition. Brooklyn-based rapper and producer Kota the Friend and Brown University professor Kevin Quashie explore Black creative sovereignty and authentic personal storytelling, using Kota’s song “For Colored Boys” as a focal point to examine Black identity through themes of fatherhood, community, and self-expression.”

Thursday, September 3

🐀 Pilot Mag x SRC: If You Win the Rat Race, You’re Still a Rat
7–8:30pm | Secret Riso Club need address, Brooklyn | $17.19

“A Talk and Discussion with Dagny Tepper, founder of Pilot Magazine, reflecting on philosophies that shape creative lives — and the convictions that made Pilot a distinct voice in contemporary culture.”

📸 “Photobooks USA” In Conversation — The Black Yearbook
6:30–8pm | ICP: 79 Essex St, Manhattan | $5 (includes gallery access)

“Join us at ICP for a conversation between Adraint Bereal, Dr. Deborah Willis, and malaika newsome on the occasion of our latest exhibition, Photobooks USA: 2000–25, featuring Bereal’s The Black Yearbook. Using the impact of the Black Photographer’s Annual as a starting point, Bereal, Willis, and newsome will discuss how frameworks such as the yearbook and family album are employed to share communal histories and its implications for the future of Black storytelling.”
