🖼️ First Friday
10am–9pm (free admission all day) | Poster House: 119 W 23rd St, Manhattan | Free

“Join Poster House on the First Friday of every month for free admission and extended hours! Explore the museum’s latest exhibitions and get in on the fun by attending a tour, workshop, performance, or activity throughout the day.” Activities include Chinese Knot Charm Drop-in Workshop and Intro to Letterpress with Jes Hughes.

🐈‍⬛ Bodega Cats of New York: A Pre-Release Slideshow and Talk
7–10pm | The City Reliquary: 370 Metropolitan Ave, Brooklyn | Free

Dan Rimada presents a pre-release slideshow and discussion from his forthcoming book about feline residents of New York’s corner stores — the cats, the stores, the people who care for them, and the legal gray area around working shop cats. The book documents sixty cats across all five boroughs, photographed by Gulce Kilkis, featuring stories from those who feed and name them.

🍰 Cake Zine: Closing Time (through Sunday)
5–6:30pm | The Glade at Little Island: W 13th St, Manhattan | Free

“An original reading series from a set of notable New York City writers about the past, present, and future of the city’s ever-changing food scene. Each 60-minute session features original stories followed by a one-of-a-kind open writing group, guided by ’s all-star authors.” Featuring , and more.

Saturday, September 5

📚 Labor Day Bookstore Sale (through Monday)
The Center for Fiction: 15 Lafayette Ave, Brooklyn | 20% off (up to 40% on select items)

“Our annual Labor Day Bookstore Sale is back! Stock up on late summer and early fall reads, knick-knacks, and more. Get 20% off in-store and online — and up to 40% off select merchandise. Also running a “Take What You Can Carry” tote bag sale: buy a CFF tote and fill it with as many books as you’d like from select carts at no extra cost.”

🎨 RU Open House Weekends (though Sunday)
11am–5pm | RU House, Colonels Row, Bldg 404B: Governors Island | Free

“On weekends in August and September, Residency Unlimited extends a warm invitation to visit the RU House on Governors Island and discover works realized in their studios by RU resident artists and local alumni.”

🦉 Wild Inside
6:40pm (95 min) | Syndicated Bar Theater Kitchen: 40 Bogart St, Brooklyn | $10

“A Eurasian Eagle-Owl named Flaco escapes from the Central Park Zoo and sets off on a magical odyssey through the island of Manhattan. Flaco overcomes his years of captivity and lack of survival skills to answer the call of the wild — and discovers he was wild inside all along.”

“At once poetic and delusional and solipsistic and beautiful... about as Romantic as it gets.” —NY Mag.

Sunday, September 6

🏄 Surf Rock 101
10:30am–8pm | Shuttle from Williamsburg to Rockaway Beach: 776 Lorimer St, Brooklyn | $20 / $65

“ Goes Surfin’ — Listen and Learn about the history of Surf Rock at our end of summer beach party! Our shuttle will take you from Williamsburg to Rockaway Beach and back. Our Sleeves listening party will be happening on the go! We’re capping off this beach day with some surf rock in action by Cliff’s Garage Band at 6pm.”

🥠 Talk Too Much 2026
11am–4pm | DCTV Firehouse: 87 Lafayette St, Manhattan | $35+

“We’re bringing hot topic Chinatown convos that mostly happen online these days — gentrification, bad landlords, too many boba shops — to a real talk panel to unpack WHAT’S REALLY GOOD.”

🚲 NYC Unifest — 17th Annual NYC Unicycle Festival (through Sunday)
Noon–5pm | 34th Ave (between 93rd & 94th St): Jackson Heights, Queens | Free

“Recreational riders, world-class performers, mountain and off-road unicycle enthusiasts, and thousands of people who haven’t ridden in umpteen years gather for “Four Days of One-Wheel Madness.” Weekend programming includes games, unicycle basketball, and a learn-to-ride area.”

🌿 Poetry in the Garden
5–6pm | Elizabeth Street Garden: Elizabeth St, Manhattan | Free

“The reading series is now accepting submissions themed around “glass.” Submissions must not exceed two pages and should be sent to art@elizabethstreetgarden.com by Friday, September 4th.”

Monday, August 24

🎾 US Open Fan Week (through Saturday)
USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center: Flushing Meadows, Queens | Free (RSVP)

During Fan Week, you register for a free pass and walk right up to the outer courts at Flushing Meadows and watch world class players practice. There’s also an extended lineup of events to check out.

🖥️ Makerspace Series / Workshop 04: 3D Rendering
6–7:30pm | Verci Flatiron: 45 E 20th St, Manhattan | $10

“Join us for the fourth workshop in our Makerspace Series! We’re celebrating the opening of our new makerspace with a series of hands-on workshops exploring different creative practices. Workshop 04: Janice will lead us through a beginner-friendly tutorial, walking step-by-step through the basics of navigating Blender and creating your first 3D render. Bring your own laptop with Blender pre-installed. Both ticket tiers require host approval to join.” Hosted at .

Tuesday, August 25

📚 Danny Ramadan + Alejandro Heredia: Crooked Teeth
7pm | Strand Book Store: 828 Broadway, Manhattan | $13.61+

“A release event featuring Syrian-Canadian author and LGBTQ+ advocate Danny Ramadan discussing his new memoir, moderated by writer Alejandro Heredia. Ramadan’s memoir chronicles his journey from Damascus through underground queer networks in the Middle East, experiences during the Arab Spring uprisings, imprisonment, and eventual arrival in Vancouver — “a powerful refutation of the oversimplified refugee narrative, a book that holds space for joy alongside sorrow, for nuance and complicated ambivalences.””

Subscribe now

🏀 Summer Movies in the Park: Space Jam — 30th Anniversary Screening
8:30pm | Fort Greene Park: Brooklyn | Free

“This iconic live-action movie features NBA superstar Michael Jordan, who is recruited by Bugs Bunny and the Looney Tunes, the Tune Squad, for a high-stakes game against an evil theme park owner and his minions, the Monstars, in outer space.”

📸 Last Sunset Tour: Aquaponics + Collaborative Cyanotype
6–9pm | Oko Rooftop at Honey’s: 99 Scott Ave, Brooklyn | $25

“This week’s sunset tour includes a collaborative cyanotype activity led by Anumeha, a photographer and filmmaker who makes site-specific portraits of local communities. Inspired by the materials and textures of the farm, Anumeha will guide you in gathering natural and found materials from around the farm — leaves, flowers, wood scraps, and more — to create a personal composition that captures your experience of the place. You’ll leave with a one-of-a-kind fine-art print.”

“Participants prepare five-minute true personal stories about the time an accident felt like fate — a misdirected journey leading to a lasting friendship, a failed interview revealing one’s true path, a serendipitous encounter with a future loved one. Sign up for a chance to tell a story or sit back and enjoy the show.”

Two downtown avant-garde fixtures — Loren Connors, the revered minimalist guitarist, and , a mainstay of NYC’s experimental/noise scene since the ‘80s.

item.content:encoded:
Monday, August 17

🎬 Dangerous Docs 2026: States of Emergency
Plaza opens 7pm, films 8:15pm | Gansevoort Plaza: 9th Ave & Gansevoort St, Manhattan | Free

“An evocative program of docu-shorts exploring catastrophe not as spectacle, but as lived experience—charting the emotional and physical aftermath of a world in constant upheaval.”

Tuesday, August 18

🎞️ Animation Nights New York (ANNY) at The Gutter Spare Room
8–10pm | The Gutter Spare Room: Williamsburg, Brooklyn | Suggested $10

“Watch a curated program of animated short films from all around the world. Animation Nights New York is a monthly screening event and annual festival based in NYC. We show the very best animated short films, virtual reality animation experiences, and interactive games from all around the world. This event is a curated monthly screening of our in-competition films.”

🎬 Seaport Cinema: Crazy Rich Asians
Movie begins at sunset (~8pm) | Heineken Riverdeck, Pier 17: 89 South St, Manhattan | Free

“Bring your own blankets and chairs to lay out on the turf. Seaport Cinema is free to attend and space is limited so arrive early to secure your spot.”

Wednesday, August 19

🪡 Fabric as Narrative: Batik + Natural Dye w/ Drishti Jaggi
5:30–8:30pm | Elizabeth Catlett Art Space & Printmaking Studio: 320 W 37th St, Manhattan | Sliding scale

This workshop introduces participants to the traditional art of batik through a contemporary, accessible, and community-centered approach. Using wax-resist techniques, participants will learn how to design and create patterns on fabric while exploring the relationship between material, memory, and storytelling. Participants will be guided through the full batik process right away from sketching ideas and applying wax resist, to layering natural or fabric-safe dyes, and finally revealing their finished textile piece.”

🎨 Inventing the Gig
7–9pm | Secret Riso Club: 122 Central Ave, Brooklyn | $54.13

“Join Secret Riso Club for a collaborative workshop making show posters for DIY music shows. We’ll explore the importance of alternative print techniques for DIY culture, especially music culture, then work in small groups to make collaborative posters for fictional bands. No Riso experience necessary. Each participants will leave with 3 copies of their one-color Riso printed poster.”

🎲 CAPICU! NYC x NuevaYorkinos Dominoes Night + Talk
7–11pm | The Lobby, Ace Hotel Brooklyn: 252 Schermerhorn St, Brooklyn| Free

“Join Capicu! NYC, NuevaYorkinos, MoCADA for an evening celebrating the stories, sounds, and traditions that shape New York’s Latine, Caribbean, and African diasporic communities. The night begins with a conversation on cultural memory, community archives, and the role of institutions in preserving the histories of New York. Following the conversation, the evening continues with domino games, a community installation, and music by Lobby resident DJ WOOF and MAMICANA.”

Thursday, August 20

📷 Yves Saint Laurent on the Page: Fashion Editorial Then and Now
6:30–8pm | International Center of Photography: 84 Ludlow St, Manhattan | $5

Inspired by Yves Saint Laurent’s relationship with magazines and press, Amanda Webster, photo editor at the New York Times’ culture desk, Noelle Lacombe, photo director at the Cut, and moderator Elizabeth Renstrom, visual artist and former senior photo editor at the New Yorker will be in conversation at ICP to discuss the world of fashion editorial then and now, and how editors approach the ever-changing future of printed media.

🌙 Night School 8.20.26
7–10:30pm | Miss Barbs: 1038 Nostrand Ave, Brooklyn | $4.99+

“Night School is a space for curious people to learn, share ideas, and build community.”

✉️ Open Studio: Letter Writing and Mail Art
6–8pm | UDP Studio: 232 3rd St #E-303, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

Inspired by our recently published title Magic Episodes and Other Synchronicities: The Transhemispheric Correspondence of Scott Burton and Eduardo Costa, 1970–1980, we encourage everybody who’s never/who’s always wanted to/who started but didn’t finish to come write and send off letters at our open studio event (stamps provided!). Alongside writing, at this open studio we will discuss and make our own mail art. Bring any desired materials (or use ours at the studio) to fold, wrap, cut, and—send away!

🪩 Late Shift: Block pARTy
5–8:30pm | Guggenheim (88th St): 1071 5th Ave, Manhattan | Free

Late Shift is hitting the streets! Join us on August 20 as we take over 88th Street for a free end-of-summer block pARTy filled with live music, art making, games, food, and drinks—all outside the Guggenheim. A stellar lineup will keep the block pARTy moving all evening, with Debit’s bass-heavy electronic grooves, followed by percussion collective A.B.E.L.A., and finally drumming ensemble Fogo Azul’s Brazilian percussion and movement.

see something interesting? invite a friend

Share

Friday, August 21

🎬 Rooftop Shots: Closing Night 2026
Doors 7:45pm, films 9pm | Green-Wood Cemetery: 500 25th St, Brooklyn | $25

For the grand finale of Rooftop’s 30th season, seven bold new short films take on love, loss, ambition, identity, and the strange, exhilarating business of being human. After three decades, there’s only one thing left to do: celebrate.

🔮 Tarot Readings with Meg Jones Wall
5:30–8pm | The Morgan Library & Museum: 225 Madison Ave, Manhattan | $10

In celebration of the exhibition Tarot! Renaissance Symbols, Modern Visions, Meg Jones Wall offers tarot readings in one of the Morgan’s historic rooms. Each reading will last 10 minutes. Readings will start at 5:30 PM and the last reading will end at 7:40 PM. Individual readings only; no group readings offered.

Saturday, August 22

🎨 Screen Printing Day
12–4pm | Sea & Soil Coop: 388 Atlantic Ave, Brooklyn | $4

“SCREEN PRINTING DAY!!!! We will have many a sea & soil screen available from our archive of screens you can print on cloth you bring or buy some for cheap! We will have a small ink fee of $4.”

🧵 Stabby Stab: Needle Felting Creatures with J Hann
3–5:30pm | Tiny Arts Supply: 612 Woodward Ave, Queens (Ridgewood) | $65 (sliding scale)

“Let’s do some needle felting! Or “stabby stab” as we like to call it. Students will learn the basic techniques of needle felting (aka “stabby stab”) in this hands-on workshop. Using a barbed needle to poke wool we will make fantastical critters (or cursed ones) to give to a friend, rest on a shelf, or more! Students will also learn what supplies are needed, the different types of needles and wool, etc.. should they choose to continue to explore this stabby art form at home! All materials provided, no experience necessary.”

🎖️ Battle of Brooklyn 250th Anniversary Reenactment
10am–12pm | Prospect Park, Long Meadow | Free

Step back in time with Prospect Park Alliance for a historic re-enactment honoring the 250th Anniversary of the Battle of Brooklyn. Join the Prospect Park Alliance, the Old Stone House of Brooklyn and the Brigade of the American Revolution to commemorate the 250th Anniversary of the Battle of Brooklyn, the largest battle of the American War for Independence. Please be advised that this battle reenactment will feature loud sounds and smoke.

🏛️ Walking Tour: Historic Buildings and New Interventions in SoHo
11am–1pm | Departs Center for Architecture: Manhattan (SoHo) | $30

The SoHo-Cast Iron Historic District, created in 1973, is dominated by remarkably intact mid-19th century architecture. Originally designed for both commercial and manufacturing uses, most of these buildings have been adapted for residential use. Meanwhile, over the last three decades, several entirely new buildings have been approved by the NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission as “appropriate” for inclusion within the district. This tour looks at these recent buildings as well as significant historic sites to examine a range of design strategies for historic districts.

Sunday, August 23

🌷 Poetry in the Garden
5–6pm | Elizabeth Street Garden: Elizabeth Street, Manhattan | Free

“We are now accepting submissions for Poetry in the Garden at Elizabeth Street Garden on Sunday, August 23rd, at 5 p.m. The next submission theme is “blue.” The submission deadline is Friday, August 21st. Please email submissions to art@elizabethstreetgarden.com. Submissions should be no more than two pages long.”

🍰 Yoga and Cake: Sweet Vinyasa
1:30–3:30pm (class begins 1:45) | Kala Yoga: 783 Driggs Ave, Brooklyn | $26

“60 minute flow x 1 slice of cake. Class will include a dynamic, playful flow that’s welcoming to all levels. We’ll move through a nourishing practice that’s both energizing and grounding. After Savasana, homemade cake. Flavor inspiration includes sweet corn, blueberry, mascarpone.”

🎖️ The Battle of Brooklyn 250: The Meaning of Freedom
10am–1pm | Green-Wood Cemetery: 500 25th St, Brooklyn | Free

“Come gather where this country began. Two hundred and fifty years ago, parts of the first major battle of the Revolutionary War was fought on land that is now Green-Wood, and we’re marking the anniversary with our biggest Battle of Brooklyn event ever! Immerse yourself in August 1776 through costumed interpreters, civilian and soldier stories, diverse perspectives on this pivotal moment, and a special parade and commemoration ceremony.”

item.content:encoded:
Monday, August 10

📚 Franklin Park Reading Series: Powerhouse Women
8pm | Franklin Park: 618 St. Johns Place, Brooklyn | Free

“Join us for a star-studded lineup of Powerhouse Women — Deb Olin Unferth (Earth 7), Julie Buntin (Famous Men), (That May Not Mean What You Think), Patricia Park (Ambrosia Lee Drops the Mic), Daikon (New Skin), and (Talking to the Wolf), sharing newly released fiction! Mingle with fellow lit enthusiasts, enjoy cheap brews, and get a shot at our readers’ latest books in our free-to-enter raffle!”

Tuesday, August 11

🎞️ Exhibition Opening: When The Camera Looks
6–8pm | Strother School of Radical Attention: 55 Washington St #736, Brooklyn | Free

“Join us to celebrate the opening of our summer show, When The Camera Looks, featuring short films by Claudia Claremi and The Friends of Attention that re-encounter the camera and screen as technologies altering our relationship to space and time. Anthesis (2023) and The Mirror Image: Attention and Infinite Reflection (2022) each document outdoor gatherings where The Friends of Attention activated protocols engaging with the technological conditions of filming and film-making. In the spirit of these experimental gatherings, we will invite you to a small indoor picnic with a flower arrangement table.”

📚 André Aciman & Sarah Maxwell-McNicol: Call Me by Your Name
6–7pm | Brooklyn Public Library, Brooklyn Heights Branch: 286 Cadman Plaza West, Brooklyn

“A modern classic reimagined: a sundrenched graphic novel adaptation of one of the greatest love stories of our time. On the Italian Riviera, Elio welcomes his father’s house guest. Oliver is the picture of arrogance – all billowing shirts and snide comments – and Elio is convinced that Oliver will be someone he’ll grow to hate. Thrown together, a friendship blossoms as the pair spend endless hours walking treelined streets, enjoying sun-soaked lunches, and besting each other at tennis.”

Wednesday, August 12

📖 Reading 101: One-Year Anniversary
Doors 6:30, readings 7pm | Night Club 101: 101 Avenue A, Manhattan

“READING 101 celebrates its one-year anniversary. Readings from , Tony Tulathimutte, Hannah Aizenman, , and Rachel Stone. Music by DJ Jago.”

🎭 International Puppet Fringe NYC — Opening Night (through Aug 16)
6pm | The Clemente: 107 Suffolk St, Manhattan | Price varies

“The International Puppet Fringe Festival, New York’s only international fringe festival dedicated to puppetry, returns August 12th to 16th, 2026, and will once again feature performances by leading puppet makers and troupes from around the world. Produced by Teatro SEA and Grupo Morán (The Morán Group) with the support of The Clemente Soto Vélez Cultural & Education Center.”

🚦 Changing Lanes: Screening and Q&A
6:30–8:30pm | SVA Theatre: 333 W 23rd St, Manhattan | $15

“What does it look like when a neighborhood fights to make its streets safer? Changing Lanes follows the multi-year effort to transform Brooklyn’s notoriously dangerous McGuinness Boulevard and how its redesign—from a four-lane boulevard into a safer, two-lane street with protected bike lanes—became a political flashpoint within the community. Filmed over the course of three years spanning the Adams and Mamdani administrations, the documentary captures a fascinating story of democracy at street level.”

Subscribe now

Thursday, August 13

👗 Fashion in Frame: Yves Saint Laurent’s Designs and Photography
6:30–8pm | ICP: 84 Ludlow St, Manhattan | $5

“Join us at ICP for a conversation between fashion historian Raissa Bretaña and ICP Creative Director David Campany on the occasion of ICP’s latest exhibition, Yves Saint Laurent and Photography. Bretaña and Campany will discuss the visual trajectory of Saint Laurent’s career, including his debut haute couture collection in 1962, his foray into film with projects such as Belle du Jour, as well as his ever-increasing presence in front of the camera.”

🔤 Czechoslovak Lettering Tour with Paul Shaw
6:30–7:30pm | Poster House: 119 W 23rd St, Manhattan | $20

“Join design historian Paul Shaw at Poster House for a tour of From Monarchy to Modernity: Travel, Identity, & the Czechoslovak First Republic (1918–1938), focused specifically on lettering. Explore how artists and designers used expressive typographic styles to shape ideas about travel, national identity, and contemporary life. Whether you’re a type enthusiast or new to lettering, you’ll discover fascinating details about the forms, techniques, and cultural context behind the bold, modern lines and colors of Czechoslovakia’s golden age of posters.”

🍷 Poetry and Pours: A Wine and Poetry Tasting
7–9pm | June Wine Bar: Cobble Hill, Brooklyn | $80 ($75pp for Date Night pair)

“Can wine help you taste language? Come find out at Poetry & Pours, an immersive experience that explores the way both wine and poetry can awaken and transform the senses. The event will feature a tasting menu of five seasonal wines from June, a natural wine bar in Cobble Hill, paired with poems hand-selected by local poets and Stephanie Niu to highlight the sensory qualities, mood, and notes of each glass.”

📺 Emmy’s Round Table and Q & A Panel
6 - 8pm | W New York - Times Square: 1567 Broadway, Manhattan | Free RSVP

“As Emmy season heats up, W New York – Times Square is bringing the pros behind this year’s most talked-about TV straight to the Theater District. On Thursday, August 13th at 6pm, the property will host a live Round Table + Q&A featuring Emmy Award winners and nominees from fan favorites shows including Hacks, Beef, SNL, Sirens, and The Penguin.”

Monday, August 3

🤠 Buck Wild Line Dancing
6–9pm | Domino Square: 12 South 3rd Street, Brooklyn | Free with RSVP

“Grab your boots and hop on down to Domino Square for a night of line dancing outdoors, hosted by Sugarfoot & Spitfire of Buck Wild. Open to all skill levels!”

Tuesday, August 4

📖 I Don’t Think About Being Great: Selected Writings by Robert Rauschenberg
6–7:30pm | The Phyllis Harriman Mason Gallery: 215 West 57th Street, Manhattan | Donation

“Discover the central role that writing played in the work of one of America’s most innovative and influential artists with Francine Snyder, Director of Archives at the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and editor of I Don’t Think About Being Great: Selected Writings by Robert Rauschenberg (Yale University Press, 2025). Snyder will be joined by artists Alteronce Gumby and Evan Yee.”

📚 Kathryn Jezer-Morton and Delia Cai
7–8pm | McNally Jackson Seaport: 4 Fulton Street, Manhattan | $5+

“An eye-opening look at how social media shapes the stories we tell and the lives we lead. Over the past two decades, platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok have revolutionized how we document and share our lives. In The Story of Your Life, journalist and New York magazine columnist examines how these algorithm-driven platforms not only change the way we share information but also shape the content itself. What stories do we choose to tell, and how do these choices reflect and shape our evolving identities?” Kathryn is joined by .

📖 Melissa Febos & Tara Westover
7–8pm | McNally Jackson Books at BKLYN Studios: 1 Dekalb Ave, Brooklyn | $10+

“From , the national bestselling author of Girlhood, comes an examination of the solitude, freedoms, and feminist heroes she discovered during a year of celibacy and a wise and transformative look at relationships and self-knowledge. Her year of divestment transformed her relationships with friends and peers, her spirituality, her creative practice, and, most of all, her relationship to herself. Blending intimate personal narrative and incisive cultural criticism, The Dry Season tells a story that’s as much about celibacy as its inverse: pleasure, desire, fulfillment.”

🎞️ Modern Silent Shorts: On Tour
8pm | : 159 Pioneer St, Brooklyn | Free

“Since 2023, Modern Silent Shorts has commissioned exciting, young directors to create new works of silent film. This screening will include 7 films from Modern Silent Shorts, ranging from animation to horror to slapstick comedy. The screening will be accompanied by live original orchestration performed by Greg Pease, Ryan Vinh, Athos Maelstrom, and composer Kevin Donald.”

Wednesday, August 5

🎙️ Lectures on Tap: “The Gamblification of Sports: Betting & Addiction”
6:30–8:30pm | Williamsburg, Brooklyn | $41.32

“In this lecture, Professor Gina Antoniello takes audiences inside the rapidly evolving marketplace of fandom, drawing on her work with SafeBets and her research at the intersection of sport, ethics, and enterprise. She asks a critical question: when sport becomes a market, who is that market really built to serve?”

🎬 In the Mood for Trivia — AAIFF49 Trivia Night presented by MUBI
8:30pm | Sugar Mouse: 47 3rd Ave, Manhattan | Pay what you can

AAIFF49 (Asian CineVision’s Asian American International Film Festival, running since 1978) tests your film knowledge with a visual round of movie posters, a soundtrack round, notable quotes, and more.

Subscribe now

Thursday, August 6

🍔 Big Vegan BBQ with Russell Markus
6pm | Public Records: 233 Butler St, Brooklyn | $19.57

Monday, July 20

🛣️ Nerd Night: Open Streets 101
6:15–8pm | Heart of Gold: 37-14 31st Ave, Astoria, Queens | Free (RSVP)

“Ever wondered how Open Streets work, why people love them, or why they’re sometimes controversial? Join us for Nerd Night, a casual monthly series bringing together people who care about New York City, public space, transportation, and community. This month’s topic is Open Streets 101—a look at how Open Streets work, what they’ve accomplished, and what’s next. We’ll cover the basics, share stories from organizers, answer questions, and leave plenty of time to meet neighbors and fellow city nerds.”

Tuesday, July 21

📚 Colson Whitehead
7–8:30pm | McNally Jackson Books at BKLYN STUDIOS: 1 Dekalb Ave, Brooklyn | $10+

“From #1 New York Times bestselling author and two-time Pulitzer winner Colson Whitehead, an exuberantly entertaining novel that brings to life 1980s New York in the magnificent final volume of his Harlem Trilogy. 1981: New York City is beginning to emerge from financial ruin and decline, energized by rampant real estate development and a Wall Street unchained by Reagan-era predatory capitalism… Whitehead paints a portrait of a city in transition, where shimmering skyscrapers rise to the heavens as displaced people huddle in abandoned tunnels below.”

📖 Olio Read-in: Kafka’s Metamorphosis
7:30–9:30pm | The Lighthouse: 603 Bergen St, Brooklyn | $32.29

“As Gregor Samsa awoke one morning from uneasy dreams he found himself transformed in his bed into a gigantic insect.” The enigmatic opening sentence of Kafka’s Metamorphosis has been perplexing translators, inspiring illustrators, and intriguing psychiatrists for over a century… In this Olio Read-in, we will be performing a close reading of Part 1 of Metamorphosis. By focusing on minuscule details—linguistic choices, floor plans, food crumbs—we will enter Kafka’s nightmarish universe that is strikingly similar to our own.”

🪩 Triple Canopy Summer Party 2026
7–10pm | Spring: 116 Madison St, Manhattan | Free (RSVP)

“Cool off with us to celebrate the summer—while supporting the magazine! 7:30pm | David Rubenstein Atrium, Lincoln Center: 1887 Broadway, Manhattan | Free

“Ian Chang is a virtuosic, genre-agnostic percussionist, composer, and producer who manipulates sound samples into a seamless synthesis of raw intensity and sophisticated sound design. Since joining eclectic trio Son Lux in 2014 and supporting artists such as Moses Sumney, Matthew Dear, and CHVRCHES, Chang’s debut 2020 full-length record, 属 Belonging, offered deeper insight into his unique and ever-evolving vision. Chang is an in-demand soundtrack artist who scored the 2022 Best Picture Oscar winner Everything Everywhere All at Once with Son Lux.”

Subscribe now

Hear from researchers working at the intersection of entomology, urban ecology, and conservation. item.title: What Are You Doing Tonight?
item.description: My thoughts after curating New York events every week for the last year.
item.dc:creator: field notes nyc | Danielle
item.content:encoded:
We’ve all seen the photo that sums up the summer energy in NYC: some guy projecting the Knicks’ game onto the side of a building, and a crowd of strangers cheering at the wall. You could pay thousands to be in MSG, but getting out on the streets is free, and way more fun. In the hundreds of events I sift through during my weekly curation, this is a trend I keep noticing. The most alive gatherings in New York right now aren’t the expensive, produced ones. They’re the DIY ones that get people out of their apartments.

Anything can be a gathering

Look-alike contests aside, the hottest event in town might be smoking a cigarette together in Washington Square Park or a literary reading in a bathhouse. At times, these discordant pairings feel like somebody has spun two wheels and concocted a random event. As these events get more absurd, I keep thinking about the way "primitive" furniture and surrealist fashion photography (à la Szilveszter Makó) are showing up everywhere in design right now. It’s part of a broader response to the rise of AI — we’re craving anything non-formulaic or imprinted with human touch. The same goes for the way we socialize.

These one-off events are novel and make for a fun story when someone asks you what you did that weekend, but alone they don’t build a fulfilling social calendar. Instead, the most engaging events are the ones where you share part of yourself or leave with plans to come back.

The best event in NYC might be three blocks away

I admire my friends who traverse multiple boroughs for an after-work gathering. I’m not built like that, and I suspect a lot of us aren’t — which is exactly why the neighborhood gathering keeps winning. Fort Greene Walking Club and Crown Heights Walking Club were started in the last couple months and I love the concept because it really can be that simple!! Get outside, meet your neighbors.

Post-pandemic, we were all about hosting elaborate dinner parties. These days, it feels like there are hardly enough hours in a week so casual hangouts are a blessing. The simplicity of the event lets us focus more on being present: these types of gatherings meet us where we are on a weekday evening (figuratively and quite literally), and they occur at a recurring time (typically earlier in the week) so we’re likely to see the same faces.

Neighborhood businesses are catching on too. We have the privilege of thousands of cafes and bars and restaurants here — so how does a small place keep people coming back? Programming: film screenings, game nights, lectures at the mom-and-pop shop. To find what's happening on your specific block, check in with your local small businesses, follow a neighborhood Substack, or ask the field notes community.

The compounding effect

A spectacle is buzzy because it happens once, but a gathering you can reproduce turns its guests into its next hosts. Green Tile Social Club and Pawn Chess Club are a couple examples of event hosts that have popularized social game-playing. Bring in a DJ, make it a meet cute, and suddenly it’s a night out. These events can sell out, but their popularity has inspired new organizers to come into the space and host, so there’s always enough game playing to go around.

Thanks to pandemic lockdowns, in a couple of years I've accumulated crochet hooks, knitting needles, a sewing machine, air-dry clay, and watercolors. Even though I’m still limited to knitting rectangular patterns, I can say that I’ve learned something new and am inspired to tackle more challenging projects. The world of crafting is so vast, so we’re finding new outlets to dabble in now that knitting clubs and collaging workshops are commonplace. I love that we’re going further and further down the rabbit hole — cyanotyping, metalworking and Armenian needlelace just to name a few.

Showing up

The events that stick are the ones that ask something of you, and give something back because of it. Whether it’s the endorphins from getting off the couch for a walk on Monday evening, a new skill from trying a finicky craft or getting to know your community by volunteering, there’s certainly no shortage of things to do!

Thank you to everyone who is organizing events for their communities 💐💐💐.
It can be scary starting off and not knowing if anyone else will show up, and there’s a lot of unglamorous behind-the-scenes logistical work.
